They harden through the effect of heat when the bodyshell goes into the ovens during the painting cycle. The sealants are applied using an extrusion or spray gun. After hardening they have the appearance of a flexible mass adhering to the panel and perform sound insulation and sealing functions protecting the panel joins from water, air and dust. Lastly, they are painted using the special products in the painting cycle. PROTECTION OF THE BODYSHELL The vehicle body is designed to withstand for many years any environmental attack to the interior, not visible but potential subject to corrosion, and exterior, particularly subject to damage that may affect the exerior appearance of the vehicle. This result is achieved through the extensive use of galvanized and double galvanized panels and by carrying out multiple treatments on all the surfaces. Galvanising The panels may be zinc coated by means of two different technological processes: deposition of zinc through galvanizing process deposition of zinc through fire In the deposition during the galvanizing process the panel comes into contact with (in the case of a single layer of zinc) or is immersed in (in the case of double galvanizing) a solution of zinc salts; a layer of pure zinc with a high level surface finish is deposited through the electrolytic effect. In fire deposition the molten zinc is deposited on the panel through a thermal effect; in this process zinc thicknesses of up to 20 micron can be reached, compared with 8 microns normally achieved through the galvanizing process. Iin the presence of water and together with the iron in the panel, the layer of zinc produces an electric torque with an electrical potential that prevents the oxidation of the iron. On this vehicle 82% of the bodyshell is made up of galvanized panels, divided between 55% of double galvanized panels and 27% single galvanized panels. After the galvanizing treatment the bodyshell is subjected to bonderization (a treatment that cleanses the panels of any greases or surface oxidation) and to cataphoresis, a fundamental treatment for protection, above all of the areas affected by welding, and subsequent painting. All the joins between the body panels are carefully sealed to prevent penetration. Painting Painting is designed to protect the panels and maintain a good aesthetic appearance (bright, shiny colour) over a period of time. The vehicle comes in a range of 5 pastel colours and 5 metallic colours. All the pastel colours except white have a double layer (opaque base coat + clear coat). The design of the vehicle gives it a unique personality with all the bodywork variants that respond to the multitude of different usages. At the front the grille and the headlamps are surrounded by plastic that protects against impacts at low speed. The side panel features the rounded shape of the windows in the front doors and the extensive rear glass which produce a sensation of light and brightness that contributes to driving comfort. The sliding side doors, the two rear asymmetrical doors or the tailgate do not alter the sense of harmony of the model but fit in naturally with the exterior design of the vehicle. The bodyshell of the veihcle has been designed for controlled deformation in the case of front, side and rear impact and to absorb the energy developed by the impact without adversely affecting the vital spaces in the passenger compartment. BENDING AND TORSIONAL STRENGTH The high torsional and bending strength of the bodyshell guarantees the vehicle excellent passive resistance qualities producing a sensation of solidness and comfort when driving. These excellent values also guarantee that the original specifications of the bodyshell are maintained over a period of time and there are no structural weaknesses that could adversely affect safety. Like 3 + sliding side doors 1890 RESISTANCE TO FRONT IMPACTS The main operations to the bodyshell for resistance to front impacts involve: front crossmember crash-box bonnet retaining hooks reinforcements on struts reinforcements on front pillars RESISTANCE TO FRONT IMPACTS The vehicle comforms with front impact standard ECE R94 with the barrier offset in relation to the axis of the vehicle (cover of front section equal to 40%) at 56 Km/h In this test checks are carried out on both structural measurements (made on the vehicle) and biomechanical ones (made on the occupant); the effects on the occupant are measured using special dummies. Front crossmember View of front crossmember with crash-box Front crossmember The front crossmember and the crash-box are a new feature in the range of group vehicles because the structural elements are integrated and fitted on the bodyshell using bolts. They have been designed to reduce repair costs following impacts at low speed. In the case of a front impact at 16 km/h with an offset barrier (front covering of the vehicle equal to 40%) only these two components are deformed. The particular shape of the crossmember and the material from which it is made (highly resistant steel) guarantee that with this type of impact there is the minimum intrusion protecting the mechanical components. If the body is repaired, the structural reinforcements should always be replaced if deformed. RESISTANCE TO SIDE IMPACTS In the case of side impacts the bodyshell is capable of offering a high level of safety, providing programmed deformation which does not adversely affect the survival chamber. The above has been achieved by: reinforcing the centre pillar adopting connecting ribs between the side pillars with the anti-intrusion bars and waist reinforcements on the doors RESISTANCE TO SIDE IMPACTS The vehicle conforms to side impact regulation ECE R 95 against a deformable barrier (centred in relation to the front seat positioned midway and adjusted to the lowest position) at 50 Km/h. If the body is repaired, the structural reinforcements should always be replaced if deformed. RESISTANCE TO REAR IMPACTS The main operations to the bodyshell for resistance to rear impacts involve: rear crossmember crash-box reinforcements on floor panel RESISTANCE TO REAR IMPACTS The vehicle conforms to the "Japanese" rear impact standards against a rigid barrier at 50 Km/h (covering of the rear of the vehicle equal to 100%). RESISTANCE TO REAR IMPACTS The rear crossmember and the crash-box are a new feature in the range of group vehicles because the structural elements are integrated and fitted on the bodyshell using bolts. They have been designed to reduce repair costs following impacts at low speed. In the case of a rear impact at 16 km/h against an offset barrier (rear covering of the vehicle equal to 40%) the floor panel is not deformed. If the body is repaired, the structural reinforcements should always be replaced if deformed. The improvement in driving comfort, in terms of quietness and quality inside the passenger compartment, has been mainly achieved through working on the following areas where noise is produced: rolling engine aerodynamic All the engine types used on the vehicle belong to a new generation with technological features designed to improve acoustics and vibrations. This same concept it also valid for the drive transmission components, the suspension and the bodyshell mountings. Diagram showing internal noise figures for slow acceleration in 5th speed: SOUND INSULATION Diagram showing application of sound insulation and thermo-expandable products SOUND INSULATION The sound insulation material mainly comprises bitumen. Their task is to dampen the noise coming from mechanical vibrations in areas such as, for example, the underbody and the interior of the doors. The thermo-expandable materials are made up of rubbers or synthetic resins and have the task of damping the box sections to eliminate acoustic propagation (noise, whilstling). When the bodyshell goes in the ovens during the painting cycle these materials expand and vulcanize adhering to the inner surfaces of the panels with which they come into contact, completely filling the box section cavities. taking into consideration the high level of acoustic comfort achieved, the specifications adopted during manufacture must be restored exactly in the event of repair. During starting, the air bag failure warning light comes on and remains on for more than 4 seconds (after the control unit initial test, the warning light should go out) In the case of a reasonably serious impact which has caused the activation of the complete system (Air Bag and Side Bag), the warning light stays on. The control unit memory cannot be cleared, so the control unit must always be replaced. If, on the other hand, only the pretensioners or the Side Bags have been activated, the memory can be cancelled using the diagnostic equipment (Examiner or other instruments) twice. All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Closely observe the following precautions when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that an extinguisher is at hand in the work area. For some procedures, the use of special tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains particular precautions to prevent a dangerous situation from arising. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 471992). Measure the pump supply voltage at the pump connector. Meaure the pump absorption current by positioning the ammeter clip for the Examiner on the pump supply cable (on the fuse box or directly on the pump inlet cable. The current measured should be between 2 and 10 Ampere.
Disconnect the electrical connection for the solenoid valve on the methane canister and check that the coil winding resistance is 11.50 Ohm ± 20 % at 20°C

1) Select methane operation. 2) Keeping the engine on, raise the vehicle on the lift. 3) Close all the canister taps except for one (work in order starting with the one on the left). 4) Wait for about 1 minute. 5) If the vehicle does not switch over to petrol start again from point 3) leaving another tap open and keeping all the others closed. 6) If the vehicle switches over to petrol this means that the canister solenoid valve with the tap open is stuck closed. Then proceed to activate it through the active diagnosis, check the wiring/connections and, if necessary, check the coil resistance.
Disconnect the electrical connection for the solenoid valve at the reduction unit and check that the coil winding resistance is 8 Ohm ±20% at 20°C

Place the three way connector 1870685000 between the low pressure pipe and the methane distribution manifold (after having moved the power assisted steering fluid reservoir to the side); Connect a pressure gauge with a 1/2' socket and 16 bar end of scale. Let the engine run normally on methane and check that the pressure is between 8 and 10 bar. If the value is lower, also check that the pressure upstream of the reduction unit is more than 15 bar. If this is the case, replace the reduction unit.

The electrical check is carried out placing a bridge (2) to be constructed locally (not available as spares) between the sensor (1) and the connector (3) in such a way as to supply the sensor and measure the output signal using a multimeter (voltmeter). Place the bridge between the sensor and the connector. Check that with the ignition ON the sensor supply is about 5 Volt. Check that there is an output voltage of between 0.5 V (with the tank full) and 4.5 V with the canisters completely full with a pressure of 200 bar.
Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position. Disconnect the electrical connection for the injector. Check that the coil resistance is 4.6 Ohm ± 10% at 20°C

Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Select 'methane gas injection' in the 'Control Unit Test' ambient. Identify the item 'Methane pressure' under the parameters. With the engine running, measure the pressure and check that it is above 10 bar with the canisters almost empty and a maximum of 220 bar with the canisters completely full. It should be remembered that the pressure in the canisters is also affected by the ambient temperature - if the temperature is low, the pressure is less.

The safety instructions described in the manual must be followed when working on the methane system components. Keep devices at high temperatures or those which could cause electrical sparks away. Let the engine run for a few minutes on methane. Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. Disconnect the battery negative terminal. Disconnect the connectors (1) from the methane injectors. Remove the methane pipe (2) retaining bands from the injectors. Remove the methane distribution manifold keeping the low pressure pipe and the injectors connected. Introduce a small amount of oil into the injector spray duct. Check that there are no gas leaks shown by a series of oil bubbles.

The test should take place in an ambient where there are no sudden variations in temperature. Transfer the vehicle to a special pneumatic test area. Close the methane canister manual valves so that they are excluded from the circuit. Connect the Examiner to the methane control unit and enter the 'Parameters' ambient to read the high pressure value. Wait for 3 minutes and then take the pressure reading again. The final pressure value should not differ from the value read (0 - 1 bar). If the initial value has changed, continue the check for another 3 minutes. If the pressure continues to fall, use the leak detector or a foam solution to check the joins (points 1-2-3-4-5-6-7-8 in the enclosed diagram). Replace the faulty components and recheck the seal. With the circuit pressurized, check the low pressure pipes and the circuit: (points 9-10-11 in the enclosed diagram). Replace the faulty components and check again that the connectors that were leaking are closed and repeat the leakage test. 1 - Pressurizing filler complete with one-way valve and safety cap 2 - High pressure pipe connector 3 - One-way valve fitted on the solenoid valve 4 - Cut out solenoid valve on the canister complete with manual cut out valve 5 - Canisters 6 - Seal between canister and solenoid valve 7 - Coated steel pipe 4 x 6 8 - Pressure regulator/reduction unit complete with pressure sensor and cut out solenoid valve 9 - Flexible pipe 10 - Methane fuel manifold 11 - Methane injectors

With the key in the ON position, all the gas/petrol selector LEDs remain on, as a diagnostic function, for around 4 secs. Supply check: With the Examiner in the 'Instrument' ambient in the 'Voltmeter' function check that, with the ignition ON, the Gas/Petrol selector receives a supply (voltage of + 5 Volt) at the Metatron 5D0 control unit, between pins 16 and 22. Gas level signal check: With the Examiner in the 'Voltmeter' function, select the end of scale value at 20 Volt and the basic time of 1 second and, with the ignition key in the ON position, connect the positive Examiner probe to pin 60 of the Metatron 5D0 control unit and the negative probe to the vehicle earth. Press the Start icon and check that there is a square wave signal with variable PWM at the Gas level Gas/petrol operating mode check: With the Examiner in the voltmeter function, check that with the ignition key in the ON position and the Gas/Petrol selector switched to 'Gas', there is an input voltage of +5 Volt at the Metatron 5D0 control unit at pin 47 and the green LED for the gas operating mode is on. Place the selector in the 'Petrol' position and check that there is a voltage of 0 Volt at pin 47 and that the yellow LED for petrol operation is lit up. Check that with the Gas/Petrol selector switched to 'Gas', there is a 'High' signal (more than 3.5 Volt) at the Metatron 5D0 control unit at pin 10 and that the green LED lights up. Place the selector in the 'Petrol' position and check that there is a 'Low' voltage signal (less than 3.5 Volt) and that the yellow LED lights up. A - Metatron 5D0 control unit B - Gas/Petrol selector

Connect the pressure transducer of the Examiner/SDC diagnostic instrument between the fuel return manifold (1a) and the return pipe to the tank (1b). Turn the ignition on (MAR). Check that, within 30 seconds, the pressure gauge's reading is less than 1 bar. The fuel pump in the tank stops after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and adjustment screws next to the pressure gauge are open (except those on pipes not connected to the system).

Connect the pressure transducer of the Examiner/SDC diagnostic instrument between the diesel filter (1a) and the pressure pump (1b). Turn the ignition on (MAR). Check, within 30 seconds, that the pressure gauge's reading is between 1.8 and 3.0 bar. The pump in the tank stops after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and adjustment screws next to the pressure gauge are open (except those on pipes not connected to the system).

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the fuel injectors. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the fuel injectors. Block the pipe so that no fuel can come out during the test. Turn the ignition key to the start position for 5 seconds and visually inspect that the quantity of recirculation fuel which comes out of the injector connections is more or less the same for all of them, and is very little.

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the fuel injectors. Connect the diagnostic equipment (Examiner or Examiner Plus) Display the 'measure diesel pressure' and 'engine rpm' parameters on the parameters screen of the Control Unit Tests. Turn the ignition key to the start (AVV) position for 5 seconds and check that the fuel pressure is over 300 bar with engine speed of about 200 rpm.

Disconnect the pressure sensor from the inlet manifold. Connect tool no. 1.870.752.000 to the inlet manifold. Reconnect the pressure sensor to the other end of the tool. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the Examiner/Examiner Plus diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and connect it. Select the 'pressure gauge' instrument on the Examiner/Examiner Plus and set it to acquire data in 'inlet pressure' mode with full scale of 2000 mmHg and time selection 10 seconds. Go out onto the road (observing the legal speed limits) and carry out the following test. On a stretch of motorway, drive the car at 2000 rpm in 4th gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part (*), excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 1900-2100 mbar (1444-1596 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 900-1100 mbar. On a fast non-urban journey, drive the car at 2000 rpm in 3rd gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part (*), excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 1900-2100 mbar (1444-1596 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 900-1100 mbar.

Basic operation Place the vehicle on a ramp. Working via the engine compartment, disconnect the battery. Remove any intake circuit sleeve. Fit buffer C10125 in the sleeve and secure it using a band. Raise the car. Remove the bolts fixing the catalyzer to the centre silencer, remove the two catalyzer support bolts and lower it . 1072C16 exhaust manifold with catalytic converter - r r Fit buffer C10126 Connect the air intake pipe to the pressure regulator network. Close the regulator tap and set it to a pressure of 0.4 bar. Connect the regulator outlet pipe to the buffer C10126. Open the regulator tap. Check for any air leaks, through a decrease in pressure. Locate the leaks using special foam.

Basic operation Check 1st stage (approx. 2.5 bar): Disconnect the pressure switch from its pipe 5040B14 air conditioner system multi-level pressure switch - r+r Disconnect pressure switch electrical connection and ensure that the circuit is open between pins 1 and 2 Disconnect pressure switch from the pipe and check for breaks in the circuit between pins 1 and 2 Reconnect the electrical connection of the pressure switch and start up the air conditioner. Wait a few minutes, making sure that the compressor switches on normally. The calibration of the 1st stage is: contact opens 2.1-2.8 bar and contact closes 2.3 - 2.9 bar. Check 2nd level (approx. 15 bar): Operate the system with the car at a standstill. Wait a few minutes; the contact between pins 3 and 4 should close. At the same time make sure that the fan comes on at the first speed. 2nd level setting is: contact closes 14.2 - 16.2 bar, contact opens 10.3 - 12.3 bar. Checking 3rd level (approx. 20 bar): Again operate the system with the car at a standstill. Wait a few minutes. Contact between pins 4 and 6 closes At the same time make sure that the fan changes from the first to the second speed. 3rd level setting is: contact closed 18.8 - 21.2 bar, contact open 13.8 - 18.2 bar. Check 4th level (approx. 28 bar): It is advisable not to allow the pressure of the circuit to increase to that value, which is too close to the safety limits. If the system should reach this level, the contact between pins 1 and 2 would open. The calibration of this level cannot therefore be checked on the car. 4th level setting is: contact open 26 - 30 bar, contact closed 18 - 26 bar.

Basic operation The test must be carried out at an ambient temperature of between 20°Χ ανδ 30°Χ. Close all the doors and windows. Set the gearbox to neutral. Start the engine and run it at a speed of 1250-1300 rpm. Open the central air vents and position a thermometer probe inside. Set the temperature selector to the coldest setting. Set the fan speed selector to 2nd speed. Set the distribution selector to the 'front' position. Activate the air conditioner. Activate recirculation Check that within 2-4 minutes the thermometer's temperature reading stabilizes at 8°-11°C.

Basic operation The test must be carried out at an ambient temperature of between 20°Χ ανδ 30°Χ. Close all the doors and windows. Set the gearbox to neutral. Connect the recharging device to the air conditioning system [5040A10] in order to read the low pressure and high pressure values. Start the engine and run it at a speed of 1250-1300 rpm. Set the temperature selector to the coldest setting. Set the fan speed selector to 2nd speed. Set the distribution selector to the 'front' position. Ensure the air conditioner is off. Activate recirculation Check on both pressure gauges of the recharging system that the pressures reach the value of 5-6 bar (higher values correspond to external temperatures higher than 30° C). Activate the air conditioner. Check that within 1 minute the low pressure reaches 2.5 - 3 bar and 15 - 16 bar on the high pressure gauge. Wait for the engine cooling fan to come on. Check that the pressure reaches 1.5 - 1.8 bar on the low pressure gauge and 10 - 12 bar on the high pressure gauge . Once this pressure is reached, the fan should go off and the low pressure reading should return to 2.5 - 3.0 bars, while the high pressure reading should return to 15 - 16 bars (if ambient temperature is higher than 25° C, the fan may stay on all the time). If the pressures are correct, but the air temperature at the outlets is high. See Test 5040 - See Test 5040C - If low pressure is 4 - 6 bars and high pressure is 20 - 25 bars with a high temperature at the air outlets. See Test 5040 - See Test 5040A -

Measure a resistance of 3.55 10% ohm between terminals 1-4 (1st speed) Measure a resistance of 1.35 10% ohm between terminals 2-4 (2nd speed) Measure a resistance of 0.35 10% ohm between terminals 3-4 (3rd speed) The resistor is cut out for the 4th speed

Basic operation Once the error has been cancelled, if the check shows that the error has not reappeared then the test is over. Disconnect the driver side air bag connector and activate the line closure resistor, with resistance at 2 Ohm. Delete the error and check that it has disappeared using a testing device such as Examiner. Reconnect the driver side bag connector Disconnect the connector from the clock spring and activate the relevant line closure resistor Delete the error and check that it has disappeared using a testing device such as Examiner. Reconnect the clock spring connector Check the condition of the wiring: there should be no interruptions or DC. If there are no faults, the control unit is faulty.

Basic operation Once the error has been deleted, if the check shows that the error has not reappeared then the test is over. Disconnect the bag connector on the line involved and activate the relevant line closure resistor. Delete the error and check that it has disappeared using a testing device such as Examiner. Reconnect the bag connector. Check the continuity of the wiring from the control unit comb to the bag connector; there should be no breaks or short circuits. If there are no faults, the control unit is faulty.

Basic operation Check the continuity of the wiring between the side bag sensor and the control unit: there should be no breaks or short circuits. Check the side sensor is working properly. if everything is working properly, there is a fault in the control unit.

Basic operation Check the continuity of the wiring for the control unit connector on the light connection panel connector: there should be no interruptions. With the ignition on, check the instrument panel is being supplied correctly.

Basic operation Once the error has been deleted, if the check shows that the error has not reappeared then the test is over. Disconnect the connectors for the pretensioners and connect the special line closure resistor. Delete the error and check that it has disappeared using a testing device such as Examiner. If the error disappears, the pretensioner is defective. If the error is still present, check the continuity of the wiring from the control unit comb to the bag connector; there should be no breaks or short circuits. Before replacing the control unit, check that the defect is not in the other pretensioner by running the full test. If there are no faults, the control unit is faulty.

All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Follow these precautions scrupulously when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. Make sure that there is a fire extinguisher in the vicinity. For some procedures, the use of special tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 47/1992). Engine oil, brake and clutch fluid, power steering fluid and engine coolant are harmful to the skin: reduce contact with the skin to a minimum, and in the event of contact, wash with soap and water. The fluid (electrolyte) contained in the battery is poisonous and corrosive. Avoid contact with the skin or eyes. Do not allow naked flames or possible sources of sparks to come near the battery: risk of explosion or fire. Oils (engine, gearbox and differential), fluids (brake and clutch, pwer steering, coolant), the battery and replaced oil and diesel filters contain substances which are harmful to the environment: they must be deposited in special containers. All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During refitting operations, replace gaskets, oil seals, spring washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts and any worn parts.

Below is a list of instructions which must, under all circumstances, be observed during any operations on vehicles equipped with LPG systems. The presence of two one-way valves prevents accidental emergence of gas from the cylinders. Fuor solenoid valves are present (one solenoid for the cylinder and one on the pressure reduction unit) which isolate the two sections of the supply pipe when the supply is selected in petrol mode or when the engine is switched off. A manual methane cut out tap is located on each solenoid. Its opening/closure permits or prevents the exit or entry of methane from the canister. Although the methane system has many safety features, you are advised to shut off the manual cock of each individual cylinder whenever the vehicle is garaged for a long period, transported on other means of transport or handled in emergency situations caused by faults or accidents. In spite of the presence of these devices it is necessary to remember that, in ambient conditions, methane is a highly flammable gas; in the presence of potential leaks during maintenance operations to the system, always follow these precautions: do not smoke no naked flames; do not use electric tools and driers. do not use incandescent lamps; do not wear acryclic clothes which produce static electricity; always disconnect battery terminals. do not use workshop equipment such as: air compressors, current generators, exhaust fans, electric tools, etc. which could produce sparks and, if there were leaks, cause an explosion. do not use any type of exhaust fan; always work in well ventilated areas. vehicles with methane gas systems which have been in an accident or those where the seal of the system may not be intact should not be kept is sealed environments. In the case of interventions on components of the CNG system, it is necessary, for safety reasons, to carry out the following procedures to drain the high and/or low pressure systems. PROCEDURE FOR DRAINING HIGH PRESSURE CIRCUIT Disconnect the battery negative terminal. Shut the manual valves located on the CNG cylinder assembly. Disconnect the electrical connection of the pressure sensor located on the pressure reducer. Using the CNG/methane switch located on the central tunnel, select the Methane starting mode. Connect the battery negative terminal. Start the engine and wait for it to stall. Connect the electrical connection of the pressure sensor. Connect the Examiner diagnostic station and check that the methane pressure in the pipe is nearly zero. Using the Examiner, delete any errors stored in the control unit's memory. PROCEDURE FOR DRAINING LOW PRESSURE CIRCUIT Disconnect the battery negative terminal. Disconnect the connection of the methane cut-off solenoid located on the reduction unit. Using the CNG/methane switch located on the central tunnel, select Methane starting mode. Connect the battery negative terminal. Start the engine and wait for it to stall. Repeat the engine starting and wait for it to stall again, to eliminate the residual gas in the pipes. Improper engine stalling could cause the control unit to store certain errors in memory (petrol pump relay error, injector relay error, etc.). Proceed with the service intervention to be conducted on the vehicle, making sure to wear the special helmet with visor conforming to UNI standards. When unscrewing the connectors, even if the internal pressure has discharged, make sure you do not come directly into contact with the jet of CNG present in the pipe. At the end of the service intervention, remember to delete any errors in the control unit's memory.

After any maintenance or replacement operation which has involved adjusting the connectors or moving the pressurized components, a search for methane gas (CNG) leaks should be carried out proceeding as described below. Road test the vehicle by driving for about 5-10 km in the methane operating mode. Return the vehicle to the workshop and place it on a lift. The test should take place in an ambient where there are no sudden variations in temperature. Close the methane canister manual valves so that they are excluded from the circuit. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and enter the 'Parameters' environment to read the high pressure value. Wait for 3 minutes and then take the pressure reading again. The final pressure value should not differ from the first value read (0 - 1 bar). If the reading is different from the initial pressure value, continue the check for a further 3 minutes. 1. If the pressure continues to fall, use an electronic meter (GAS DETECTOR L.P.G. - CNG - GIGATRON or similar device) to search for gas leaks, testing each component and each individual pipe in the CNG system: cut-off solenoid on cylinder complete with manual cut-off valve (1a), (1b) and (1c), one-way valve (1d), three-way connector (1e), recharging filler complete with non-return valve and safety cap (1f), recharging pipe connecting sleeve (1g), steel pipes (1h), pressure reducer complete with pressure sensor and cut-off solenoid (1i). Identify the section of the system where the leak is coming from using the electronic detector, then apply the leak-detecting foam to the components (BRC code 90AV99000052 or a similar product) in order to identify the exact point where the gas is escaping. Repair the component involved, checking the cause of the leak (connectors not properly tightened, seals not replaced, defects in the part). Repeat the procedure again to check for leaks until the problem is fully resolved. 2. With the circuit under pressure, check the circuit and the low-pressure pipes: flexible pipe (2a), methane fuel manifold (2b) and methane injectors (2c). Identify the section of the system where the leak is coming from, using an electronic detector as described above, and take the appropriate corrective action (tighten connectors, replace seals or replace the part). Repeat the procedure again to check for leaks until the problem is fully resolved.

The manual procedure and the teser procedure for re-initalising the electronic ignition/injection control unit is shown below. When the car is first started, carry out the following operations whenever the throttle body or engine management unit is replaced. During this procedure, from the moment when the instrument panel is supplied with power until the end of learning, do not press the accelerator, brake or clutch pedals. Procedure using tester Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position. Connect the tool to the tester input and place the knob in position 3. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Turn the ignition key to ON position Wait for the test to be run on the throttle body, when the tester will confirm that Turn the ignition key to the OFF position Using the Examiner, check that the self-learning of idle speed has finished correctly ( LOWER THROTTLE BED SELFLEARNING- completed) If the self-learning procedure is not correct, turn the ignition off (STOP position) and repeat the above procecure. If the incorrectness continues, check that the diagnostic cable connection is secure and that the instrument is working. Manual procedure Turn the ignition key to ON position Wait 60 seconds, the time required for the control unit to check the throttle body's internal spring and the butterfly's maximum/minimum angles. Turn the ignition key to the OFF position Wait 10 seconds, the time required for the control unit to save the learnt values in EPROM. After carrying out the initialisation procedure, the power supply may be disconnected from the engine control unit (battery disconnection) without losing data.

Start the engine and warm up until the radiator cooling fan comes on for the second time. Leave as little time as possible between the engine preheating stage and the moment the test begins and avoid a prolonged idling period. Check that sensor diameter is at least 0.22 times exhaust pipe diameter. Ensure that the exhaust gas uptake fitting joints are effective enough to prevent leaks. Position the fume measurement device sensor in the exhaust tail-pipe. Take care that the end is placed in a pipe section where the gas flow is uniformly distributed. If necessary, to meet the above requirements, fit an exhaust pipe extension so that the exhaust pipe coupling is sealed and the sensor end is located in a straight section at least six times as long as the exhaust tail-pipe diameter toward the engine and at least three times the tail-pipe diameter downstream. Check that the sensor sampling pipe from the exhaust tail-pipe to the fume measurement device, is on an upward slope and does not include acute angled kinks. Ensure that the counter-pressure to the sensor is as specified and does not exceed 7.5 mbar during the test. With the engine on and idling, place the gearbox in neutral and release the clutch pedal. Position the fume measurement meter to allow the sampling of exhaust gases. Record the reading shown on the fume meter gauge. As the engine is idling, rapidly and gently pump the accelerator pedal until the engine is turning at maximum speed and the governor cuts in. Record and note the maximum fume value marked on the fume meter during the acceleration without considering values during the overrunning stage. As soon as the maximum rotation speed is reached, release the accelerator pedal until the engine is idling again. Check that the fume meter point returns to the position corresponding to the idling reading. Repeat the above operations at least six times until the fume readings entered have stabilised. The readings are considered to have stabilised when four consecutive readings are within a 0.25 m -1 range and are not in decreasing order. The fume values to be considered are the arithmetic mean of the four stabilised values. Check that the calculated fume value complies with the specified value printed on the vehicle marking summary plate located in the engine bay and indicated in the table below. Measurement Value - Exhaust fumes (m¯ 1) 1.30 Start up the engine and let it reach operating temperature. Connect the opacity meter pipe for measuring the exhaust gases to the end section of the exhaust pipe. Carry out the opacity meter connections and adjustments following the Manufacturer's instructions. Fully depress the accelerator pedal three times, in quick succession in order to reach the speed at which the engine rpm restricter intervenes. Take measurements for five successive full accelerations and make a note of the maximum values reached. To obtain the value for the test, take the arithmetical average of the three closest figures (from the five taken). If there is more than one suitable trio, select the one which gives the highest average value and check that it is within the recommended limits. Measurement Value - Exhaust fumes (-) < 70% Start up the engine and let it reach operating temperature. Connect the opacity meter pipe for measuring the exhaust gases to the end section of the exhaust pipe. Carry out the opacity meter connections and adjustments following the Manufacturer's instructions. Fully depress the accelerator pedal three times, in quick succession in order to reach the speed at which the engine rpm restricter intervenes. Take measurements for five successive full accelerations and make a note of the maximum values reached. To obtain the value for the test, take the arithmetical average of the three closest figures (from the five taken). If there is more than one suitable trio, select the one which gives the highest average value and check that it is within the recommended limits. Measurement Value - Exhaust fumes (-) </= 70%

Carry out the measurement with all the emission control devices active and at the specified idle speed. - Insert the probe of an exhaust gas analyser into the end of the exhaust pipe for at least 30 cm. If the shape of the exhaust tailpipe will not allow the probe to be fully introduced, add an extension that ensures a seal in the joint area. - Wait for the exhaust gas tester indices to stabilise. - With the engine idling, check that the CO2 level is within specified limits. All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Closely observe the following precautions when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that an extinguisher is at hand in the work area. For some procedures, the use of special Fiat tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 47/1992). All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. Avoid brake - clutch fluid coming into contact with paintwork; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Do not reuse brake-clutch fluid drained during bleeding. Turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down. In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nut and all components which have deteriorated.

All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Closely observe the following precautions when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that an extinguisher is at hand in the work area. For some procedures, the use of special Fiat tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 47/1992). All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. Avoid brake - clutch fluid coming into contact with paintwork; If this should happen, wash immediately with water. Do not reuse brake-clutch fluid drained during bleeding. Turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down. In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nut and all components which have deteriorated.

All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Closely observe the following precautions when carrying out operations in the engine compartment: Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that an extinguisher is at hand in the work area. For some procedures, the use of special Fiat tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 47/1992). All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. During refitting, lubricate the parts as necessary to prevent seizure during the initial period of operation. When refitting, it is essential to respect tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nut and all components which have deteriorated.

Clearance due to wear is taken up automatically The handbrake should only be adjusted after having replaced the rear brake shoes, the rear brake cylinder and the cable assembly. Proceed with the adjustment when the vehicle is on the lift. 1. Remove cover (1a) from central tunnel (1b). 2. Make a note of the position of the nut, then loosen the adjustment nut (2a) for the handbrake cable by at least two or three turns to ensure that the cable (2b) is completely loosened. Start the engine. With the engine idling, press the brake pedal forcefully at least 10 or 15 times. Retighten the handbrake cable adjustment nut to the original position. Make sure that, with the handbrake lever in the rest position, the rear wheels can rotate freely. Check that the braking action of the handbrake starts before the first notch. At the end of the adjustment, check that the lever does not travel through more than five notches of the toothed sector. Turn off the engine. Refit the cover on the central tunnel. Remove the car from the lift.

All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Closely observe the following precautions when carrying out operations in the engine compartment. Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that an extinguisher is at hand in the work area. For some procedures, the use of special Fiat tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 47/1992). All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nut and all components which have deteriorated.

All operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid injury to persons. The engine compartment contains numerous moving parts, components at high temperatures and electrical wiring with voltage. Closely observe the following precautions when carrying out operations in the engine compartment. Switch off the engine and wait for it to cool down. Do not smoke. No naked flames. Make sure that an extinguisher is at hand in the work area. For some procedures, the use of special Fiat tools is indicated. The use of these tools is vital in order to work safely. Follow the safety instructions in force for workshop procedures. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific warnings to prevent the risk of dangerous situations. When using chemicals, closely follow the safety instructions given on the safety sheet which the supplier must give to the user (in Italy, in accordance with D.M. no. 47/1992). All the operations must be carried out with the utmost attention and care to avoid damaging the components. In order to release parts which are sticking, apply gentle blows using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved: use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts. During dismantling, check that parts which have to be marked carry reference marks. When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent sticking or seizing during the initial operating period. During refitting, it is essential to observe the tightening torques and adjustment data. During each refitting, replace the gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nut and all components which have deteriorated.

Removing Refitting Position the starter motor in the vice fitted with protective jaws. 1. Undo the nut (1a) and disconnect the electrical supply terminal (1b). 2. Undo the nuts fixing the starter motor solenoid. 1. Remove the fixed section of the solenoid. 2. Remove the spring. 3. Remove the moving section of the solenoid. Refitting Removing Clean the components with compressed air and a clean cloth (do not use liquid detergents). Lubricate the sliding surfaces of the moving parts with grease and fix the solenoid. Position the vehicle complete with spare wheel, tools, fluids, fuel reserve and with the driver on board. Check that the tyre inflation pressure is correct. Place the headlamp alignment control switch in position "0". Place the vehicle on a flat surface, perpendicular to a screen with an opaque surface 10 metres away on which the following lines are traced. 1. V-V: vertical, corresponding to the trace of vehicle plane of symmetry. 2. C-C: traces of vertical planes passing through the reference centres of the light clusters. 3. HC-HC: horizontal corresponding to the height from the ground of the reference centres for the light clusters. 4. AC-AC: horizontal 13 cm below the line HC - HC. 5. Lines inclined by 15° as illustrated in the diagram. Switch on the dipped headlamps. 1. Vertical alignment. Adjust the vertical adjustment screw for the light cluster so that the horizontal section of the demarcation line between the dark zone and the area lit up by the light band is aligned with the line AC - AC traced on the screen. 2. Horizontal alignment. Adjust the horizontal adjustment screw for the light cluster so that the point where the two horizontal and inclined demarcation lines cross with the point where lines C - C and AC - AC cross on the screen are aligned.

To be followed only for individual devices equipped with their own adjustment systems. Position the vehicle complete with spare wheel, tools, fluids, fuel reserve and with the driver on board. Switch the fog lights on and, working via the opening (1a) in the lower part of the bumper, adjust the adjustment pin (1b) to position the headlamp so that on a screen positioned 10 metres away the demarcation line is lower than the reference centre of the fog lights equal to the value recommended for the dipped headlamp light beam for the vehicle in question plus 1/3 of the height of the centre of the fog light from the ground. If the angle is such that the beam hits the ground before the screen, correct the alignment upwards so that the demarcation line hits the ground at the point where the screen is, i.e. 10 metres from the front of the vehicle. Before removing and refitting the Air Bag module, the following preliminary operations must be carried out: (1) turn the ignition off ('STOP'); (2) disconnect and isolate the battery cables; (3) wait 10 minutes before proceeding. CLOSELY FOLLOW ALL THE RECOMMENDED SAFETY RULES ( Op. 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM see assembly 5580C Air Bag System) Removing Refitting 1. Use tool (1a) to prise open studs (1b) and remove control unit protection (1c). Name Country 1a Scraper blade 1.878.077.000 2. Disconnect electrical connectors (2a), unscrew retaining bolts (2b) and remove air bag control unit (2c). Name Connector 2a Air Bag control unit See M060 AIR BAG CONTROL UNIT Refitting Removing Follow these precautions: never strike or shake the control unit; do not connect the electrical connection to the control unit before having fixed the control unit correctly; Ensure that the battery leads are disconnected in all cases. If the control unit is being replaced, remove the removable part of the adhesive label from the new control unit and place it in a special file containing the vehicle details (model, registration date, chassis number) and the serial number of the old control unit. This file should be kept for future checks. Fit the air bag control unit and secure with bolts. Connect the Air Bag control unit electrical connection. Name Connector - Air Bag control unit See M060 AIR BAG CONTROL UNIT Fit the airbag control unit and secure with the studs. Connect the battery leads. Check system operation using an Examiner tester.

General safety warnings The activities connected with repairing the bodywork involve the use of equipment and tools in addition to the handling of chemical products and substances for which the supplier's instructions must be followed. It is therefore necessary to pay special attention to: The correct use of materials, instruments and equipment: before carrying out any sort of operation, read the instruction manuals carefully and follow the accident prevention and safety instructions with great care. The workplaces for carrying out operations, which should have appropriate ventilation systems which satisfy the legal requirements concerning air exchange, the filtration of harmful substances (solvents) and the reduction of dust levels. The handling of dangerous substances which should be carried out in accordance with the supplier's instructions and recommendations. The collection and disposal of refuse which should be carried out in accordance with the laws in force. When working with and handling harmful and dangerous substances, the appropriate safety equipment should be employed (clothing, masks, gloves, goggles, etc.). Vehicle repair operating cycles The vehicle repair operating cycles usually consist of the following stages: checking the vehicle measurements; cutting/removing damaged elements and preparing the bodyshell for welding; welding replacement elements; preparing for painting; painting; renewing the anti-corrosion treatments; sound insulation, sealants. CHECKING AND RESTORING THE VEHICLE MEASUREMENTS This is the first stage in the repair process in which the distortion suffered by the bodyshell is measured and evaluated and the components involved are identified. During this stage the first actual repair operation is carried out: pulling the bodyshell to restore the measurements before cutting and removing the damaged elements. PULLING THE BODYSHELL Pulling the bodyshell, to restore the measurements, is carried out on straightening benchs where it is possible to secure the bodyshell using vices and attachments which should be fixed according to specific methods for each vehicle, with instructions provided by each supplier. Jigs are used to check the measurements of the bodyshell. They are positioned at specified points, and are used to check the measurements indicated by the jig manufacturer for each model, or alternatively the vehicle's own measurements given in the section 'Descriptions and Operation'. Example of a possible straightening bench configuration. General repair instructions . Before carrying out any sort of operation on the vehicle, disconnect the battery terminals. For safety reasons and for a better quality repair, IT IS PROHIBITED TO: replace structural parts of the bodyshell without using a repair bench. The use of the bench makes it possible to guarantee the restructuring of the vehicle with the original manufacturing measurements, ensuring the correct position of the forecarriage and back-carriage elements. heat the structural parts of the bodyshell to straighten them. cut and weld, edge to edge, any bodywork element and reinforcement on the same line. Remove the damaged elements, cutting them on the joins, following the cutting lines given in the Service Manual. Carried out correctly, the operation involves wasting a few centimetres between the two cutting lines in order to improve the distribution of the fusible points created by the welding. The diagram below illustrates a possible implementation. General repair instructions . The removal of the damaged elements is the repair operation during which the potentially most dangerous equipment is used. Before carrying out any operation, read the safety instructions in the manual very carefully and follow the warnings from the manufacturer of the equipment in conjunction with the safety and accident prevention recommendations. The use of the following is required for the removal of damaged body panels: hack-sawing machines; circular saws; power chisels (only in case of need); plasma-arc cutting systems; electric drills; milling machines; grinding machines; dolly blocks and hammers; disc grinding wheels; air purifiers / extractor systems. HACK-SAWING MACHINE This type of saw makes it possible to carry out fast and precise cutting, with the possibility of regulating the speed of the blade to suit different situations. Example of the use of a hack-sawing machine OSCILLATING CIRCULAR SAW An oscillating saw is used in cases where high cutting precision is required; for example, when you need to replace the sheet metal of a box section that is laid over a panel which must not be damaged. By adjusting the speed and the number of oscillations it is possible to achieve the precision required according to the conditions of use. The high level of safety of this instrument makes it advisable to use it as an alternative to other types of saws. Example of an oscillating circular saw POWER CHISEL A pneumatic chisel is used to remove parts of body panels; it is advisable to use it: when it is not possible to use a power saw, milling machine or drill; for example, when a panel that must not be damaged lies behind the panel that requires cutting; when it is possible to directly separate the welded panels, inserting the power chisel between the two panels along the join edge in order not to leave edges which need removing later on. The different attachments increase its versatility. Example of the use of a power chisel PLASMA-ARC CUTTING SYSTEM This cutting system, achieved through the combined effect of an electric arc and gas or a mixture of gases, is used whenever it is necessary to cut rather large panels. Depending on the thickness of the panel and the depth of the cut, adjust the current and the gas flow following the instructions in the Manufacturer's booklet. The use of a plasma-arc cutting system requires the use of an extractor system to get rid of the fumes and harmful gases. DOLLY BLOCKS AND LEVERS These instruments are used when panels need to be straightened by beating, in order to have a counter-action point to support the panel. Dolly blocks are designed so that they adjust to the different panel conformations and, when the working area permits, they can replace a hammer. Levers are used in the same way as dolly blocks, however they are designed so that they can be introduced through restricted openings and spaces to get to areas which are difficult to reach. Dolly blocks and levers are also used to eliminate distortions from the edges of panels which are not removed thereby allowing correct matching with the replaced panels, avoiding weakening the structure. EQUIPMENT The following equipment is used for these operations: welding guns; seam (MIG) welders; oxyacetylene torches (brazing). INTRODUCTION TO ELECTRICAL SPOT WELDING In electrical spot welding the heat needed to melt the metal is supplied by the resistance to the current flow provided by the actual metal. Spot welding is carried out to panels where the join edges overlap and the panel metal melts; no metal filler is therefore needed for this type of welding. In areas where three or more panels overlap, spot welding should be repeated for a second time. The type of join produced is not continuous; to create a join with good mechanical strength the spot welds must be correctly spaced following precise instructions (see tables below). SPOTE WELDING In the case of spot welding, check:: that the arms are correctly aligned; that the diameter of the edges of the electrodes is correct; the planarity and that the weld edges are correctly matched; that the welding sequence is correct. Before welding, apply electro-weldable galvanizing protection to the edges of the join to protect the box sections from corrosion. Welding on this type of surface would create a concentration of tension which would result in breakage. Example of correct spot welding at corners. A. Area where welding should not be carried out. SEAM (MIG) WELDING MIG welding should be used for parts where spot welding cannot be used. When carrying out seam (MIG) welding, check: the speed that the seam weld beads have been correctly made (alternating weld sections) In this welding system (automatic advance seam) a protective inert gas atmosphere is used (hence the name M.I.G. which stands for Metal Inert Gas). The continuous progress of the seam (which constitutes both the electrode and the filler metal), allows long welds to be made without interruption. The flow of inert gas sent to the welding area eliminates the surrounding air preventing the oxidation of the metal and therefore has the function of providing a protective layer for the weld. For these reasons, MIG welding differs from welding carried out with a covered electrode through the absence of dross on the welding bead; also there are no pores which can occur during normal arc welding. The use of MIG welding requires an extractor system to get rid of the fumes and harmful gases. OPERATING METHODS In order to weld two panels correctly using a MIG welder: grind or pickle the panel thoroughly, place the equipment in a sensible position so that whilst carrying out the welding the outer casing of the torch does not become twisted or assume positions which could hinder progress, wear protective clothing and a suitable mask with non-actinic glass (glass standard no. 8 for currents of 40/60A and no. 9 for currents of 80/200A). Make sure that there is good electrical contact. Adjust the gas flow according to the instructions of the equipment Manufacturer. Make two spot welds at the two edges of the join line and one at the centre, then carry out spot welds in the middle of the two sections defined in this way. The spot welds should be 25-30 mm apart. The diagram below illustrates correct welding. the correct gap is about 1 mm. Carrying out a weld using inert gas (MIG) for joining two matched panels. OPERATING METHODS It is not advisable to initially carry out a seam weld because, in addition to being difficult to do, it can cause distortion of the panel through the accumulation of heat involved. The difficulty in carrying out a weld with a single bead lies in the need to move the torch fairly slowly in order to achieve good weld penetration which is also quick enough not to incur the risk of 'burning' the panel. Moving the torch too quickly also results in a poor weld bead content because after the subsequent operations of grinding the bead the layer of material remaining is not sufficient to guarantee the resistance of the join. After the initial spot welding of the panel, the spot welds should be ground to the level of the panel using a rigid disc grinder. At this point the alignment of the panels should be checked and, if necessary, corrected using a hammer and steel dolly block. Then proceed with filling the gaps between the various spot welds carrying out alternating welding sections, keeping the torch at an angle of around 60°, (see diagram above). 1. Tacking the join. The fact that the weld has been carried out correctly is confirmed from the rear of the weld bead which should show a series of spherical bumps along the entire length of the join. The MIG welder can also be used for joining overlapping panels where only one side is accessible. To carry out the welding, the panels must adhere perfectly and the torch should be kept perpendicular to the surface. In this way the action of the electrode melts the first panel initially, then the second producing a crater which is filled. In order to carry out this operation correctly, the welding machine must be adjusted to the correct current value for the thickness of the panels being worked on and pressure must be applied to the surface, with the torch resting on its supports, to faciliate the matching of the panels. AIR FILTRATION AND PURIFICATION SYSTEM When carrying out operations which produce fumes, gases and dust which is dangerous to the operator, air filtration and purification systems must be used. These systems are adapted to suit the varying requirements and their size depends on the volume of air to be purified. These systems usually operate through the combined action of mechanical and electro-static filtration and purification through active charcoal. Filtration takes place in two stages: mechanical elimination, using wire gauze, of the largest particles of dust subjecting the flow of air to ionization which statically charges the particles of dust which are then eliminated from the flow through the electro-static process. The air flow is then purified by passing through active charcoal filters. In addition to their efficiency, handling and noise levels in these systems has been improved so that they never create a nuisance. Example of a portable air filtration and penetration system Introduction Painting the bodyshell has two fundamental objectives; protecting the surfaces of the panels from environmental attack and, from an aesthetic point of view, producing a shiny, bright colour. The large number of chemical products used in painting operations requires special care to be taken over their handling and usage. These painting operations involve the emission of paint fumes and solvent vapours which, if inhaled by the operators, can seriously affect their health and they should only be carried out in special spray booths. The operator should always wear a mask and protective clothing. These masks can be the filtration type for brief operations and the total protection pressurized type for longer operations. EQUIPMENT The following equipment is used during painting operations: filltration masks and protective clothing; masking materials and tape; spray booths and drying ovens; spray guns; infra-red lamps; polishers; PROTECTIVE CLOTHING When carrying out painting operations, suitable clothing should always be worn, so that the operator is well protected from contact with harmful agents. It is also advisable to use a barrier cream applied to the most exposed uncovered areas (face, hands and arms) which should be removed at the end of the painting operations. be removed at the end of the painting operations. FILTRATION MASK This type of mask only protects the operator's respiratory tracts, so goggles and hair protection should also be used at the same time. Its use is recommended for small retouching operations. Example of a filtration mask. PRESSURIZED MASK This mask guarantees protection of both the face and hair and is supplied with pure air via the compressed air system which operates the spray gun. The air is further purified with a degree of separation approaching 100% by an active charcoal filter fitted to the operator's belt. The slight excess pressure created inside the helmet prevents the infiltration of paint vapours. The use of this mask is advisable for lengthy painting operations. Example of a pressurized mask SPRAY BOOTH Painting and drying operations for prepared parts should be carried out in spray booths. If the extent of the damage repaired is medium to large, it is advisable to use a special spray booth and a hot air oven for drying the paint. The workplace must be equipped with an air conditoning system and filtered by purifiers, mainly consisting of renewable active charcoal filters. consisting of renewable active charcoal filters. The optimum painting conditions which should be maintained in the booth during painting are as follows: constant temperature of between 22 -25 ° ? constant humidity of between 75-80% The workplace in question can be: a combined type spray booth and drying oven; a separate type spray booth and drying oven. SPRAY GUNS The development of ergonomics and spraying techniques has led to the definition of a new type high air volume and low atomization pressure spray gun where the paint mist is considerably reduced. This type of spray gun is lighter with a grip designed to reduce tiredness and the onset of cramp and has a trigger which requires far less effort than traditional spray guns. The handling of the spray gun has also been made easier through the balance and the reduced visual restriction which allows greater control when working. The most interesting aspect of this spray gun is the supply system which allows painting in any direction, even with the reservoir pointing downwards, also improving cleaning procedures with a considerable saving in time and materials. The possibility of painting from above or below in addition to preventing the formation of areas which are either too wet or too dry, facilitates access to areas of the bodywork which are difficult to reach. Special attention has been paid to the ease of adjustment which requires minimal, simple movements. This type of gun combines great efficiency with a very refined atomization capacity for any produce, even those which are water-soluble and is used at pressures of 0.7 g (10 PSI) or less. Thanks to these capacities for exploiting the painting material, considerable savings are achieved in financial terms and the working environment is improved. Use from the top to the bottom PORTABLE INFRA-RED LAMPS If the operation only involves small retouches, the use of a drying oven is not advisable. In these cases the paint can be dried using special infra-red lamps fitted on parabolid mirrors. The use of one or more lamps positioned in such a way that an even temperature is produced on the surface of the area retouched, allows the drying of the paint film and produces results which are comparable to those obtained in drying ovens. These types of lamps considerably reduce the drying times, also reducing energy consumption. The lamp should only be used when the paint has undergone a degree of drying so that it is 'outside the powder' condition. For normal clear coat: spray a light coat followed by two coats at intervals of several minutes. 23. Description The entire electrical system has been designed and constructed in accordance with the most up-to-date guidelines concerning safety and protection, especially against fire risks. There are two main kinds of protection: active protection, aimed at reducing possible causes of faults 'at source'; passive protection, aimed at minimizing the effects of a possible fault. The first category involves careful design of wiring with thorough positioning and anchorage. Wiring is shielded and protected and the routes are carefully determined. Modifications have therefore been made to the alternator and starter motor cables, with the adoption of protective caps. Passive protection instead includes all the interventions, which have always been adopted on vehicles, to reduce high fault currents (overload and short circuit). All the fuses included in the system have been rated on the basis of the nominal absorption of the loads which cannot be served simultaneously, and so as to ensure intervention in the case of a definite short circuit. All the electrical systems are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12. V. The battery is, in turn, recharged by the alternator See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING ] during engine operation. The main supply lines are protected by fuses grouped together ina junction unit positioned near the battery and supplied directly by it. Some circuits are supplied continuously, even if the vehicle is stopped and the ignition is off, as they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied by turning the ignition key to various different positions: when the key is inserted and turned to the first click, the ignition is turned on (MAR position) and several circuits are supplied, which are thus called 'ignition-operated' (lines 'INT' and '15/54'); the second click - start up position - supplies the starter motor; (line '50')., disconnecting some circuits (those which absorb most power), thus ensuring the maximum flow of current to the starter motor; ('INT/A' line). on the other hand, by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction (and pressing the special button) the PARK position is engaged which supplies the side lights even with the key switched off ('STAZ' and 'POS' lines); See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS ]. The lines through which the supply is distributed to the various electrical devices are shown on the wiring diagrams relating to the various functions and systems. This general diagram shows all the lines which depart from the battery and the junction unit and the ignition switch; reference should be made to the specific diagrams for greater detail.

Functional description All the electrical equipment and systems are supplied by the battery A01. The supply for the various devices is controlled by two junction control units in the engine bay B01 and under the facia B02 . These contain the fuses and the relays which allow the electrical apparatus to work properly. Other circuits are supplied by turning ignition key H01 to various different positions: In the ON position, numerous circuits and services controlled by the ignition (INT line) are supplied, protected by fuses for the junction unit B01 and (line 15/54) in the AVV position - the starter motor is supplied; (line '50') See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING in the PARK position the side lights are supplied ('STAZ' and 'POS' lines); See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. Description The side lights are switched on when the ring nut on the steering column is turned to the first position, with the ignition in the ON position. They can also be turned on by extracting the key and turning it in the opposite direction - PARK position - keeping the special button pressed. Turning on the side lights also turns on the number plate lights and numerous other interior lights for passenger compartment lighting and instrument & control lighting (these lines are described and illustrated in the diagrams for the components to which they refer). The side lights switch is protected by fuses in the engine bay junction unit and in the junction unit under the facia A warning light in the instrument panel indicates that the side lights have been switched on.

Functional description The signal for activating the side lights reaches the ignition switch H01 (STAZ) connector B pin 4 from the steering column switch unit H05 when the latter is switched so that the circuit between connector B pin 5 and connector B pin 6 is closed. The supply reaches the steering column switch unit H05 from the fuse F32 housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 and from another fuse F1 contained in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . When the ignition switch H01 is in the STAZ position, the body computer receives a supply from H01 (POS) to activate the front and rear side lights and the no. plate lights via the junction unit under the dashboard B02 pin 2 connector E. The supply for the front light clusters F10 and F11 arrives from pins 40 and 30 connector C of the body computer, respectively; and for the rear light clusters F30 and F31 from pins 5 and 6 of connector A. The supply for the no. plate lights F50 and F51 is protected by fuse F51 located in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The body computer M01 is involved in supply the 'side lights on' warning light in the instrument panel E50 via connector F (pins 31 and 36). The body computer is supplied via pin 11 connector E of the junction unit B02 from the ignition switch H01 (INT) or via a line protected by fuses F53 and F1 housed in junction unit B02 and junction unit B01 , respectively and, lastly, directly by the battery via protective fuse F1 in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . The supply lines arriving from the junction unit B02 via pin 11 connector E and pin A connector C also supply the instrument panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 and F53 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.
