The side lights come on at the first click of a wheel on the stalk switch, on with key ON. They may also be turned on by removing the key and turning backward - PARK position - while keeping a special button depressed. The number plate light and numerous other interior lights for lighting the passenger compartment, instruments and controls are activated together with the side lights (these are described and explained in the wiring diagrams for the relevant components). The side light circuit is protected by special fuses located in the engine bay junction unit and in the under-facia junction unit. A warning light on the instrument panel indicates when the side lights are on. In the Comfort version of the instrument panel, a side light and number plate light check function is available. Any faults are recognised by vehicle branch (right or left side). In this case, the Body Computer sends the fault status to the instrument panel via the CAN line. An exterior lighting warning light comes on on the panel and the information is shown simultaneously on the display.

The side light activation signal reaches ignition switch H01 (STAZ) connector B pin 4 of stalk unit H05 when the stalk is switched to close the circuit between connector B pin 5 and connector B pin 6. Stalk unit H05 receives a power supply from fuse F32 in under-dashboard junction unit B02 and an additional fuse in engine compartment junction unit B01. When ignition switch H01 is set to STAZ, the body computer receives a power supply from H01 (POS) to activate the front and rear side lights and the number plate light via under-dashboard junction unit B02 pin 2 connector E. For front lights F10 and F11, the power supply is received from pins 40 and 30 connector C of the body computer; from pins 5 and 6 connector A for tail-lights F30 and F31. The power supply to number plate light unit F50 and F51 is protecteed by fuse F51 positioned in under-dashboard junction unit B02. Body computer M01 supplies the device built into instrument panel E50 via connector F (pins 31 and 36). The body computer is supplied via pin 11 connector E of junction unit B02 from ignition switch H01 (INT) and via a line protected by fuses F53 and F1 contained in control unit B02 and B01 and lastly directly from teh battery via a fuse F1 in engine compartment junction unit B01. The supply lines that reach junction unit B02 via pin 11 connector E and pin A connector C also supply control panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 and F53. Pins 8 and 9 of connector D of the body computer are earthed.

Description The vehicle has two special lamps for the dipped beam headlamps. The dipped beam headlamps are switched on through the steering column switch unit by turning the special ring nut in the position after the side lights (second position). The dipped headlamps remain on even with the main beam headlamps switched on - they go off, however, when the fog lights are switched on. The circuit is protected by two fuses, one for the right hand headlamp, one for the left hand headlamp. The dipped headlamps circuit also enables the operation of several other functions, for example, switching on the rear fog lamps and the operation of the headlamp alignment.

Functional description The activation of the dipped headlamps is controlled by an earth signal coming from the steering column switch unit H05 , by turning the ring nut, and reaches the body computer M01 at pin 4 connector D. To switch the dipped headlamps on, the body computer M01 energizes a relay R1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 which receives a direct supply, protected by fuse F1 , housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 , and sends it to the left and right headlamps. Each line is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 : F13 for the left headlamp, F12 for the right headlamp. Another supply signal 'controlled by the ignition' (INT), coming from the ignition switch H01 arrives via pin 11 connector E of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The direct signal to the left headlamp is also sent to the instrument panel E50 at pin 6 connector A for the functions that require this enablement signal. In addition, the instrument panel E50 communicates with the body computer M01 via pins 3 and 4 connector A and receives supply lines at pins 1 and 2 connector A. It then receives the earth signal at pin 7 connector A. Both the left and right headlamp signals are used to operate the headlamp alignment ( See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR ]).

The vehicle is equipped with two specific dipped beam headlamps. The dipped beams are activated by turning a wheel on the stalk switch to the next position after the side light setting (second position). The dipped beams stay on even with the main beams on and are turned off by turning on the fog lamps. The vehicle offers a follow me home function. This strategy allows the dipped beams to be kept on even with the ignition off for a preset time (within two minutes of turning off the engine). This function is particularly useful, for example, after parking the vehicle in a garage or poorly-lit places/areas. The function is activated by means of the left steering wheel stalk (light flasher): each time the stalk is operated, activation of the dipped beams is extended by 30 seconds for up to 5 minutes, after which they turn off automatically. The circuit is protected by two special fuses: one for the right headlamp and one for the left. The dipped beam circuit also enables the operation of certain other functions, e.g. rear fog lamp activation and headlamp alignment control.

The dipped beams are activated by an earth signal from stalk unit H05 when the wheel is operated and reach body computer M01 at pin 4 connector D. With the key of, pin 33 connector F of the body computer receives a signal from the stalk unit that activates the follow me home function. To turn on the dipped beams, body computer M01 activates a relay F1 contained in under-dashboard junction unit B02 that receives a direct power supply protected by fuse F1 contained in under-dashboard junction unit B01 and sends it to the two right and left headlamps. Each line is protected by a fuse in the under-dashboard junction unit B02. F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right. An ignition-controlled signal (INT) from ignition switch H01 reaches pin 11 connector E of under-dashboard junction unit B02. The direct signal to the left headlamp is also sent to instrument panel E50 at pin 7 of connector A for functions that require this enablement signal. Instrument panel E50 also communicates with body computer M01 via pins 8 and 9 connector A and receives supply lines at pins 1 and 3 connector A. It also receives an earth signal at pin 2 connector A. In the Natural Power (1.6 16v Bipower) version, the direct signal to the left headlamp is also sent to instrument panel E50 at pin 6 of connector A for functions that require this enablement signal. Instrument panel E50 also communicates with body computer M01 via pins 4 and 3 connector A and receives supply lines at pins 1 and 2 connector A. It also receives an earth signal at pin 7 connector A. The left headlamp signal and right headlamp signals are both used to operate the headlamp alignment corrector. For further details, See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR

Description The vehicle has two special lamps for the main beam headlamps. These are switched on: with the dipped beam headlamps switched on by pushing the steering column switch unit lever towards the dashboard (stable mode) in 'flash' mode, by pulling the lever towards the steering wheel (unstable mode) The circuit is protected by two fuses in the engine compartment junction unit, one for the right lamp and one for the left lamp. A warning light in the instrument panel signals that the main beam headlamps have been switched on.

Functional description The activation of the main beam headlamps is controlled by an earth signal coming from the steering column switch unit H05 by rotating a ring nut and it reaches the body computer M01 at pin 33 connector F. To switch the main beam headlamps on, the body computer M01 energizes a relay R2 , housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 , from pin 9 connector C. Another energizing signal, coming from the ignition switch H01 , reaches the relay R2 at the same time and enters pin 30 connector B of the engine compartment junction unit B01 . The latter receives the supply directly from pin 1 connector A and sends it to the right and left headlamps at the outlets at pins 22 and 25 of connector B, respectively. Each line is protected by a fuse in the engine compartment junction unit B01: F15 for the left headlamp, F14 for the right headlamp. Body computer M01 also controls the activation of the light on the instrument panel E50 . The body computer can be supplied via pin 11 connector E (supply 'controlled by the ignition') and pin A connector C (direct supply) of the junction unit B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply which is located in the junction unit B01 . These lines also supply the instrument panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 and F53 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

Description The direction indicators and hazard warning lights delimit the outer dimensions of the car. The left and right direction indicators are operated by raising or lowering the appropriate lever on the stalk unit. The hazard warning lights (right and left direction indicators operated simultaneously) are turned on by the pressing the red button at the centre of the dashboard. The turn signals are activated with the ignition key on; For safety reasons, the hazard warning lights can be turned on at any time, as they are supplied directly from the battery. The circuits for the direction indicators and hazard warning lights are protected by two different fuses. Two warning lights on the dashboard, also flashing, indicate when the left and right direction indicators are turned on - they come on simultaneously if the hazard warning lights are switched on.

Functional description The circuit is controlled by the body computer M01 which receives a signal to activate the direction indicators from both the steering column switch unit H05 (at pin 7 connector D, pin 30 connector F) and from the switch unit H90 (at pins 29 and 34 of connector F). The steering column switch unit H05 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (STAZ) at pin 5 connector B, whilst the control unit H90 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 6 connector A via a line protected by fuse F49 housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . Once the control for the direction indicators is operated, the body computer M01 is involved in supplying the appropriate direction indicators: left front light F10 from pin 38 of connector C; right front light F11 from pin 39 of connector C; left rear light F30 from pin 12 of connector A; right rear light F31 from pin 3 connector A; left side direction indicator F20 from pin 2 connector A; right side direction indicator F21 from pin 13 connector A; At the same time, the body computer M01 lights up the warning light in the instrument panel E50 via pins 5 and 6 of connector D. By pressing the switch in the control panel H90 the red LED in the actual switch which lights up the ideogram comes on intermittently. H90 supplies all the direction indicators via pins 29 and 34 of connector F entering the body computer. The supply for the body computer M1 is both controlled by the ignition and direct to pin 11 of connector E (INT) and pin A of connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . These lines also supply the instrument panel dividing into two inside the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The lines are protected by fuses F37 and F53. Description The direction indicators and hazard warning lights delimit the outer dimensions of the car. The left and right direction indicators are operated by raising or lowering the appropriate lever on the stalk unit. The hazard warning lights (right and left direction indicators operated simultaneously) are turned on by the pressing the red button at the centre of the dashboard. The turn signals are activated with the ignition key on; For safety reasons, the hazard warning lights can be turned on at any time, as they are supplied directly from the battery. The circuits for the direction indicators and hazard warning lights are protected by two different fuses. Two warning lights on the dashboard, also flashing, indicate when the left and right direction indicators are turned on - they come on simultaneously if the hazard warning lights are switched on.

Functional description The circuit is controlled by the body computer M01 which receives a signal to activate the direction indicators from both the steering column switch unit H05 (at pin 7 connector D, pin 30 connector F) and from the switch unit H90 (at pins 29 and 34 of connector F). The steering column switch unit H05 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (STAZ) at pin 5 connector B, whilst the control unit H90 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 6 connector A via a line protected by fuse F49 housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . Once the control for the direction indicators is operated, the body computer M01 is involved in supplying the appropriate direction indicators: left front light F10 from pin 38 of connector C; right front light F11 from pin 39 of connector C; left rear light F30 from pin 12 of connector A; right rear light F31 from pin 3 connector A; left side direction indicator F20 from pin 2 connector A; right side direction indicator F21 from pin 13 connector A; At the same time, the body computer M01 lights up the warning light in the instrument panel E50 via pins 5 and 6 of connector D. By pressing the switch in the control panel H90 the red LED in the actual switch which lights up the ideogram comes on intermittently. H90 supplies all the direction indicators via pins 29 and 34 of connector F entering the body computer. The supply for the body computer M01 is both controlled by the ignition and direct to pin 11 of connector E (INT) and pin A of connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . These lines also supply the instrument panel dividing into two inside the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The lines are protected by fuses F37 and F53. Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer M01 are connected to earth. This reference signal is also supplied to the panel via pin 36 of connector F of the body computer.

The flashing turn signal and hazard lights delimit the vehicle's bulk. The right and left side turn signals are activated by raising or lowering a steering wheel stalk switch. The hazard warning lights (right and left side indicators operated simultaneously) are activated by means of a red button in the centre of the control panel in the dashboard. The turn signals are ignition-operated but the hazard warning lights can always be operated for safety reasons because they are supplied directly by the battery. The turn signal and hazard warning light circuits are protected by two different fuses. Two warning lights on the instrument panel, also intermittent, indicate activation of the right and left indicators. They come on simultaneously if the hazard warning lights are activated. The Comfort instrument panel also offers a turn signal/hazard light check function. Faults are detected by vehicle branch (right and left side), in this case the Body Computer sends the fault status to the instrument panel via the CAN network, which turns on the relevant exterior light fault warning light and simultaneously shows the information on the display.

The circuit is controlled by body computer M01, which receives a turn signal activation signal from stalk unit H05 (at pin 7 connector D, at pin 30 connector F) and also from switch control unit H90 (at pins 29 and 34 connector F). Stalk unit H05 receives an ignition-operated supply (STAZ) at pin 5 connector B while control unit H90 receives an ignition-operated supply line (INT) at pin 6 connector A via a line protected by fuse F49 in under-dashboard junction unit B02. Once the turn signal control is operated, body computer M01 supplies the turn signals as appropriate. - left front headlamp F10 from pin 38 of connector C; - right front headlamp F11 from pin 39 of connector C; - left tail-light F30 from pin 12 of connector A; - right tail-light F31 from pin 3 of connector A; - left side turn signal F20 from pin 2 of connector A; - right side turn signal F21 from pin 13 of connector A; Simultaneously body computer M01 turns on the relevant warning light on instrument panel E50 via pins 5 and 6 of connector D. The red led in the switch comes on intermittently when the switch on control unit H090 is pressed. Via pins 29 and 34 connect F entering the body computer, H90 enables the power supply to all the turn signal/hazard lights. Body computer M01 is supplied via the igntion and directly at pin 11 of connector E (INT) and at pin A of connector C respectively from under-dashboard junction unit B02. Fuse F1 in junction unit B01 protects the direct power supply. These lines also supply the control panel, splitting inside under-dashboard junction unit B02. These lines are protected by fuses F37 and F53. In the Comfort version of the control panel, if the circuit or bulbs are faulty, the Body Computer communicates with the instrument panel (pins 9 and 10 of connector A) via the CAN line (pins 5 and 6 of connector I) to turn on the exterior lighting fault warning light and all the messages available on the display. Pins 8 and 9 of connector D of the body computer M01 are earthed. This reference signal is supplied to the panel via pin 36 of body computer connector F.

Description The brake lights are located at the rear in the side lights and in the central third brake light. All three bulbs are operated whenever the brake pedal is pressed, by means of a switch on the pedal itself. The centre light is operated directly, whilst the two side ones are managed by the body computer. The circuit is supplied with the ignition switched ON and is protected by a fuse, in the junction unit under the facia. A braking signal is also sent from the switch to the ABS, through the vehicle electric control system, which detects braking status and therefore introduces braking control.

Functional description The activation signal for the brake lights leaves switch I30 whose supply is controlled by the ignition via the connection between the ignition switch H01 and pin 11 connector E of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The line is protected by fuse F37 housed in the same junction unit ( B02 ). When the brake pedal I30 is pressed the switch closes and the centre rear light F40 is supplied via pin 5 connector D of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . At the same time, a signal is sent to the body computer M01 which lights up the third brake lights in the rear lights F30 and F31 from pins 32 and 22 of connector A, respectively. The body computer can be supplied via pin 11 connector E (supply controlled by the ignition) and pin A connector C (direct supply) of the junction unit B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

All three bulbs are operated each time the brake pedal is pressed via a switch on the actual pedal. The centre light is operated directly, whilst the two side lights are managed by the body computer. the switch on the pedal consists of two contacts that supply two signals: the first N.A. type recognizes the position of the brake pedal if it is different from the rest position; the second N.C. type: recognizes the position of the brake pedal in the rest position. Description The vehicle is equipped with a reversing light located in the rear lights. They are operated each time reverse gear is engaged through the special switch on the outside of the gearbox casing. The circuit is supplied with the ignition switched ON and is protected by a fuse, in the junction unit under the facia.

When reverse gear is engaged, the switch closes and the reversing lights in the right rear lights F31 and the left rear lights F30 are supplied via pin 8 of connector D of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . At the same time, this supply is sent to the body computer M01 for the connected logic functions. The body computer is supplied via pin 11 connector E of the junction unit B02 from the ignition switch H01 (INT), or via a line protected by fuses F53 and F1 housed in junction units B02 and B01 , respectively, and, lastly directly from the battery via the protective fuse F1 in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

Description The vehicle has two additional fog lamps for use in poor visibility conditions. The fog lights are activated through a special button on the switch unit in the middle of the facia. The fog lights circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a relay, both located in the junction unit in the engine compartment. The fog lights only come on when the side lights are switched on. In addition, if the key is turned ot the OFF position or the side lights are switched off, the fog lights are switched off even if the button is pressed. A warning light in the instrument panel signals that the fog lights have been switched on.

Functional description The activation signal for the fog lights consists of an earth signal coming from the switch unit H90 and entering at pin 20 of connector E of the body computer M01 . If there is a side lights signal, H90 receives a supply to light up the panel via a line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 from the line controlled by the ignition (INT). If there is a side lights signal and switch H90 is closed, the body computer M01 sends an earth signal which energizes the relay R14 , located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 , via the body computer at pin 8 connector C. At the same time, the body computer M01 also controls the switching on of the fog lamps on warning light located in the instrument panel E50 . The supply for the relay R14 is controlled by the ignition (15/54) and its outlet supplies the two fog light bulbs in the lamps: left F10 and right F11 , from pins 4 and 5 of connector B of the engine compartment junction unit B01 , respectively. The body computer can also be supplied via pin 11 connector E (supply controlled by the ignition) and pin A connector C (direct supply) of the junction unit B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the junction unit B01 . These lines also supply the instrument panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 and F53 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

The vehicle is equipped with two extra-penetration fog lamps for use in the case of poor visibility. The foglamps are operated by means of a button on the control unit in the centre of the dashboard. The fog lamp circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a relay, both located in the underfacia junction unit. The sidelights must be switched on in order to switch the fog lights on. If the ignition key is switched OFF or the side lights are turned off, the fog lights are deactivated even if the operating button is still pressed: A warning light on the instrument panel indicates foglamp activation.

The foglamp activation signal takes the form of an earth signal from switch unit H90 entering at pin 20 of connector E of body computer M01. In the presence of a side light signal (pin 2 of connector E of junction unit B02), H90 receives a power supply to light the panel via a line protected by fuse 49 of under-dashboard junction unit B02 from ignition-operated line (INT). With a side light signal and switch H90 closed, body computer M01 sends an earth signal that activates relay R14 in engine compartment junction unit B01 via the body computer outlet at pin 8 connector C. Simultaneously, body computer M01 also controls the fog lamp on warning light in instrument panel E50. Relay R14 is supplied from the ignition-operated line (15/54) and its output supplies the two foglamps in the appropriate headlamps: left F15 and right F16, respectively from pins 4 and 5 of connector B of engine compartment junction unit B01. The body computer may be supplied via pin 11 connector E (ignition-operated supply) and pin A connector C (direct power supply) of junction unit B02. The direct power supply is protected by fuse F1 in junction unit B01. These lines also supply control panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 and F53. Pins 8 and 9 of connector E of the body computer are earthed.

Description The vehicle is fitted with an extra bright rear fog lamp, located in the left rear light cluster which can be used in all poor visibility conditions. The rear fog lamps are activated by a button in the switch unit on the central console beneath the central air diffusers. The rear fog lamps are enabled when the dipped beams are on, or when the fog lights are on. A warning light in the instrument panel signals that the rear fog lamps have been switched on.

Functional description The activation signal for the rear fog lamps consists of an earth signal coming from the switch unit H90 and entering at pin 35 of connector F of the body computer M01 . H90 receives a supply for lighting up the panel from the line controlled by the ignition (INT) protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . When the button H90 is pressed, the body computer M01 lights up the rear light cluster ( F30 for the left hand drive version and F31 for the right hand drive version) via pin 31 connector A if there is a supply from the line controlled by the ignition H01 (INT) and the dipped headlamps on signal which arrives from the steering column switch unit H05 (pin 4 of connector D of the body computer). At the same time, the body computer M01 also controls the switching on of the rear fog lamps warning light located in the instrument panel E50 . The instrument panel E50 receives a supply, via the body computer M01 , through a line controlled by the ignition (pin 1 connector A) protected by fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 and from a line coming directly from the battery (pin 2 connector A) protected by fuse F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 and by fuse F1 of the engine compartment junction unit. Both lines arrive from the body computer M01 ; like the earth line (pin 7 connector A) and the serial lines at pins 4 and 3 of connector A.

The vehicle is equipped with a very bright rear fog lamp located in the rear of the left light cluster (right light cluster for right hand drive versions) and can be used in all poor visibility conditions. The rear fog lamps is activated using the special button in the switch unit in the middle of the dashboard under the centre air vents. The enablement for switching on the rear fog lamp depends on the dipped headlamps or the fog lights being in use. A warning light in the instrument panel signals that the rear fog lamps are on. The rear fog lamps check function is available on the version with a Comfort instrument panel. Any fault can be recognized by the vehicle branch (left or right side), in which case the Body Computer transmits the failure status via the CAN to the instrument panel which lights up the special "exterior lights failure" warning light and simultaneously shows the information in the display.

The rear fog lamps activation signal consists of an earth signal coming from switch unit H90 entering pin 35 of connector F of the body computer M01. The switch unit H90 receives a power supply for lighting the trim from the ignition-controlled line (INT) protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02. When the button H90 is pressed, the body computer M01 turns on the rear light cluster (F30 for left hand drive versions and F31 for right hand drive versions) via pin 31 connector A if there is a power supply from the ignition-controlled line H01 (INT) and the dipped headlamps on signal which arrives from the steering column switch unit H05 (pin 4 of connector D of the body computer). At the same time, the body computer M01 also controls the switching on of the rear fog lamps warning light located in the instrument panel E50. The instrument panel E50 receives apower supply, via the body computer M01, through an ignition-controlled line (pin 1 connector A) protected by fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 and from a line coming directly from the battery (pin 3 connector A) protected by fuse F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard and from fuse F1 of the engine compartment junction unit B01. Both lines come from the body computer M01; similarly the earth line (pin 2 connector A) and the serial lines at pins 8 and 9 of connector A. On versions with the Comfort instrument panel, if there is a failure in the circuit or the bulbs, the Body Computer notifies the instrument panel (pins 9 and 8 of connector A), via the CAN line (pins 5 and 6 of connector I) and the "exterior lights failure" warning light is switched on as well as all the available messages on the display. On the Natural Power version (1.6 16v Bipower) the instrument panel E50 communicates with the body computer M01 via pins 4 and 3 connector A and receives supply lines at pins 1 and 2 connector A; it then receives an earth signal at pin 7 connector A.

Description The front interior light includes two courtesy lights with two control switches; the rear interior light, on the other hand, has only one courtesy light. The control switches can be used to select the following operating modes for the front courtesy light: with the left switch in the centre position: the lights go on/off when the doors are opened/closed; with the left switched pushed towards the left: the lights are constantly off; with theleft switched pushed towards the right: the lights are constantly on; With the courtesy light off, the right switch can be used to switch on the left or the right light, individually, according to the position of the actual switch. Some models also have two different timing systems to make it easier to get in and out of the car. The courtesy lights come on when entering the vehicle as follows: when the front doors are opened for 15 seconds; when a door is closed (within three minutes) for seven seconds. In every case, the timing is interrupted when the ignition is switched ON. As far as the timing of the courtesy lights on leaving the vehicle is concerned (removal of the ignition key), the switching on follows this logic: within two minutes of the engine being switched off for three minutes; when a door is closed (within three minutes) for seven seconds. The timing ends automatically when the doors are locked.

Functional description The supply for the front courtesy light G10 reaches pin 2 via the body computer M01. The supply is managed through an operating logic based on the input signals at connector A of the body computer coming from: the front courtesy light G10 (pin 3) and entering at pin 21; the left front door switch I16 at pin 1; the right front door switch I17 at pin 11; the left rear door coupling D35 at pin 16; the right rear door coupling D36 at pin 26. The body computer also manages the supply for the rear courtesy light G20 via pin 33 connector A. It receives the signal from the tailgate lock I21 at pin 3. Both courtesy lights are earthed at pin 1. The supply for the body computer M01 is both controlled by the ignition and direct to pin 11 of connector E and pin A of connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth. The body computer manages the supply for the rear courtesy light G20 and the supply for the luggage compartment light ( See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT ]) at pin 33 connector A. The rear courtesy light G20 is connected at pin 3: to the tailgate lock I21 at pin 3; (pin 1 of I11 ); to the left rear door coupling D35 at pin 1; to the right rear door coupling D36 at pin 1; to the body computer at pins 16 and 26 of connector A.

Description All the instruments (dials and gauges) are lit up with the ignition switched ON. All the instrument panel LEDs are always lit up at the same brightness. The LEDs for lighting the instrument scales are activated when the side lights on message is received from the body computer.

Functional description The instrument panel E50 receives a supply via a line controlled by the ignition and directly from the battery. The former enters the instrument panel at pin 1 connector A protected by fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 coming from the body computer M01 (pin 31 connector F). The line coming directly from the battery arrives from the body computer (pin 3 connector D) at the instrument panel E50 (pin 2 connector A) and is protected by fuse F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 and by fuse F1 of the engine compartment junction unit. The instrument panel E50 and the body computer M01 also communicate with pins 3 and 4 of connector A of the instrument panel and pins 5 and 6 of connector D of the body computer. There is also an earth reference at pin 7 connector A of the instrument panel E50 which comes from pin 36 connector F of the body computer. The switching on of the LEDs inside the instrument panel is controlled directly by the body computer M01 on the basis of the signals coming from the ignition switch H01 : pin 2 of connector B of the ignition switch directs the supply line controlled by the ignition (INT), whilst pin 3 connector G directs the supply line controlled by the ignition (POS) when the steering column switch unit is turned to activate the side lights.

The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls. All instruments and controls (faces and guages) are lit up with key ON. The instrument panel leds are kept permanently on at the same brightness level. On versions with the COMFORT panel only, the brightness of the instrument scale and graph leds may be adjusted when the side lights are turned on. Eight brightness levels are offered on the COMFORT panel version, from 30% to 100% of maxmum brightness. Once the required brightness has been set, this is stored and then reused. The brightness level may be adjusted by means of two “MODE + ” and “MODE – “ keys located to the right of the instrument panel near the windscreen wash/wipe stalk only when the instrument panel is on the standard screen and the side lights are on. On versions with a COMFORT panel, when a fault message is displayed (apart from "ice danger), the display brightness is automatically set to maximum (daytime setting) even when the side lights are on. The brightness level is fixed on MODALE and STRIP panels. For further details, See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS

An ignition operated power supply (INT) from instrument E50 reaches pin 1 of connector A through body computer M01, pin 31 connector F, from a line protected by fuse F37 of under-dashboard junction unit B02. Instrument E50 is also supplied directly from the battery - pin 3 of connector A - (for Natural Power version - 1596 16V BPW - pin 2 of connector A) via the body computer, pin 3 of connector D, from a line protected by fuse F53 contained in under-dashboard junction unit B02. Body computer M01 and control panel E50 communicate with one another to exchange information on the correct operation of the devices present in the vehicle respectively from pins 5 and 6 of connector D and pins 9 and 8 of connector A (for the Natural Power version - 1596 16V BPW - pins 3 and 4 of connector A). The instrument panel is also earthed via the body computer, from pin 2 connector A (for the Natural Power version - 1596 16V BPW - pin 7 of connector A). Activation of the leds inside the instrument panel is controlled directly by body computer M01 on the basis of signals from ignition switch H01: pin 2 connector B of the ignition switch carries the igntion-operated supply line (INT) while pin 3 connector B carries the "ignition-operated" line (POS) when the stalk is operated to turn on the side lights.

Description The horns are operated by pressing one of the two sides of the steering wheel. The horn circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a specific relay located in the engine compartment junction unit. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time (even with the key removed).

Functional description The system for the horns is supplied through the horn relay R3 , located in engine compartment junction unit B01 from the direct line from the battery through the fuse F10 located in the junction unit. The coil of the relay R3 is energized by an earth signal when one of the steering switches is closed; on versions with Air Bags these connections are made via the clock spring at the steering column switch unit H05 . This signal reaches pin 21 of connector B of engine compartment junctionunit B01. The relay R3 supplies the horn P05 from pin 28 of connector B. The horn P05 and the steering column switch unit H05 are connected to earth C10 at pins 2 and 16, respectively.

Description The system operates with the ignition key turned ON. The windscreen wiper system is activated by the steering column switch unit lever on the right of the steering wheel. There are five different positions for this lever corresponding to: windscreen wiper off (standstill); intermittent operation (up to 4 types of intermittent function); continuous fast operation (1st speed); continuous fast operation (2nd speed); temporary operation (unstable lever position, lever returns to neutral position when released and automatically deactivates the windscreen wiper. The windscreen washer function is operated by pulling the lever gently towards the steering wheel: the windscreen washer pump is activated in this way; if the lever is kept in this position, the windscreen wiper comes on (continuous operation); when the lever is released, the windscreen wiper still works for a few strokes. The operation of the windscreen wiper is regulated by an electronic device incorporated in the steering column switch unit. It produces the intermittent operation and controls the operation of the actual windscreen wiper motor. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a fuse and is operated by a relay both in the junction unit under the dashboard.

Functional description The windscreen wiper switch on the steering column switch unit H05 makes it possible to select the different windscreen wash/wipe operating modes. The supply for the steering column switch unit H05 arrives at pin 11 of connector A via the outlet at pin 10 connector A of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 .Inside the junction unit B02 this line comes from the relay R12 via a line protected by fuse F43 . The supply at the relay arrives from the line protected by fuse F1 housed in the junction unit B01 from pin A connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The operation of the relay R12 is determined by the supply line controlled by the ignition (INT/A) entering the junction unit under the dashboard B02 at pin 1 connector E. Depending on the pre-selected function, the stalk unit H05 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the internal electronic device to the windscreen wiper motor N15: from pin 9 for operation at first speed; from pin 8 for operation at second speed; from pin 6 for zeroing. Stalk unit H05 also supplies windscreen/rear window wiper pump N22 by sending a supply signal and an an earth signal from pins 12 and 10 of connector A. Steering column switch unit H05 is earthed at pin 7 connector A and at pin 5 connector C. The windscreen wiper motor N15 is then connected to earth at pin 5.

This stalk may be moved to five different positions that correspond to the following functions: - windscreen wiper off (stationary); - intermittent operation (up to four types of intermittent setting are present); - continuous fast operation (1st speed); - continuous fast operation (2nd speed); - temporary operation (unstable stalk position), stalk retursn to neutral position when released and automatically deactivates the windscreen wiper. Description The rearscreen wiper is operated by turning the ring nut on the end of the lever located on the right of the steering wheel. This allows the rear wiper to work intermittently. By pushing the lever gently towards the steering wheel (unstable position) the rearscreen washer function is activated; the same pump is used as for the windscreen washer, but it rotates in the opposite direction and sends the detergent fluid to the rear. If the lever is kept pressed, the rearscreen wiper comes on and operates for a few strokes after the lever is released. The rearscreen wiper can only be operated with the ignition switched ON. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and is operated by a relay (which also controls the windscreen wash/wipe circuit) both located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The rearscreen wiper is regulated by a device inside the stalk unit.

Functional description The operation of the rearscreen wash/wipe is determined by the special switch on the steering column switch unit H05 and by the supply controlled by the ignition coming from the ignition switch H01 (INT/A). The supply at the steering column switch unit H05 reaches pin 2 of connector C via the outlet at pin 17 connector G of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 .Inside the junction unit B02 , this line arrives from the relay R12 via a line protected by fuse F52 . The supply at the relay arrives from the line protected by fuse F1 housed in the junction unit B01 from pin A connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The operation of the relay R12 is determined by the supply line controlled by the ignition (INT/A) entering the junction unit under the dashboard B02 at pin 1 connector E. The steering column switch unit H05 controls the rearscreen wiper motor N16 via two lines (pins 4 and 3 of connector C) going from the junction unit under the dashboard B02 (input: pins 15 and 11 connector G, output: pins 9 and 20 connector D). Description The rear window and door mirror heater coils are activated by a button in the switch unit in the middle of the facia. The defrosting circuit is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a relay both located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The control is deactivated in two ways: MANUALLY: by pressing the button again; AUTOMATICALLY: after 20 minutes of actual operation, i.e. with the control active. Automatic rear window heater element operation is dependent on the engine rpm signal. The activation/deactivation sequence is as follows: for the first 10 minutes the operation does not depend on the engine speed; afterwards, it depends on the operation of the engine, namely: if the engine speed is below 1000 rpm for ten seconds, the heated rear windscreen is switched off, otherwise, if the engine speed is above 1000 rpm, it remains on until it has been effectively working for twenty minutes. If the battery voltage goes below 8.5 V, the heated rear windscreen relay feed switches off the circuit.

Functional description The activation signal for defrosting the rearscreen and the door mirrors consists of an earth signal coming from the switch unit H90 entering at pin 32 of connector F of the body computer M01 . The ideogram for the switch H90 is lit up by the supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 6 via a line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . In order to activate the defrosting of the rearscreen and the rear view mirrors, the body computer M01 receives a signal from both switch H90 and the speedometer sensor K84 via pin 17 connector C. If necessary, it then energizes the relay R11 in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . Once energized, the relay R11 supplies: the left heated rear windscreen P54 and the right heated rear windscreen P53 via fuse F40 and the left P60 and right P61 mirrors via fuse F41 . Once the function is activated, the body computer M01 is involved in lghting up the warning light in the instrument panel E50 from pins 6 and 5 of connector D of the body computer. The instrument panel is earthed via the body computer, from pin 7 of connector A. The body computer can be supplied via pin 11 connector E (supply controlled by the ignition) and pin A connector C (direct supply) of the junction unit B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the junction unit B01 . These lines also supply the instrument panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 (pin 1 connector A) and F53 (pin 2 connector A). Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

Description The two external rearview mirrors are adjusted by the control located near the actual mirrors. The two mirrors are adjusted by a single button pressed in the four directions: a switch selects the right or left mirror. The button, which can be pressed in four directions, controls two electric motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor rotates the mirror on a horizontal axis, the other on a vertical axis. The adjustment circuit for the rear view mirrors is protected by a fuse located in the junction unit which protects other supplies controlled by the ignition. The adjustment is only possible with the ignition switched ON.

Functional description The two-way switch for adjusting the mirrors H30 operates two electric motors located in the left and right rear view mirrors P60 and P61 respectively. The switch receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the line for fuse F49 located in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 at pins 7 and 8 of H30 , whilst pin 5 is earthed. The switch H30 is lit up when the ignition is switched on (INT). According to the selector position, either the left motors (output signals from pins 1 and 3 of H30 ) or the right motors (output signals from pins 2 and 4 of H30 ) are connected; the common supply comes from pin 6 of H30 and is connected to pin 5 of motors P60 and P61 . Once the selector is set for the right mirror or the left mirror, the switch is operated in one direction or the other, sending the corresponding motor the positive and earth signals, thereby determining the direction of rotation. The motors which adjust the vertical position are connected to pin 4 of P60 and P61 , the motors which adjust the horizontal position are connected to pin 3.

The adjustment of the two door mirrors is achieved by means of the special control device located near the driver's mirror. Both mirrors are adjusted by means of a single button which can be pressed in four directions: this is made possible by a switch that allows either the left or the right mirror to be selected. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on a horizontal axis, the other on a vertical axis. The rear view mirror adjustment circuit is protected by a fuse located in the junction unit that also protects other ignition-controlled power supplies. The adjustment can only take place with the ignition ON.

The dual control switch for adjusting the mirrors H30 operates the two electric motors in the driver's P60 and passenger P61 exterior rear view mirrors. The switch receives an ignition-controlled power supply (INT) from the line for fuse F49 located in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 at pins 7 and 8 of H30, whils pin 5 is earthed. Switch H30 (pin 8) is lit up with the ignition on (INT). Depending on the position of the selector, the driver'sr side motors (signals coming out of pins 1 and 3 of H30) or the passenger side motors (signals coming out of pins 2 and 4 of H30) are connected; the joint power supply leaves pin 6 of H30 and is connected to pin 5 of motors P60 and P61. Once the selector is set to the driver's or passenger side mirror, the switch is activated in one direction or the other sending the motor the corresponding positive or earth signal thereby determining the direction of rotation. The motors that adjust the vertical position are connected to pin 4 of P60 and P61, those that adjust the horizontal position to pin 3.

Description The lock motors on all the doors are activated simultaneously upon a command: from the key; from the front door switches (knobs); from the remote control. Locking operation: when the key is used on one of the two front doors or the remote control is operated when the doors are firmly shut, all four doors are locked simultaneously. Unlocking operation: when the key is used on one of the two front doors, or the remote control is operated, all four doors are unlocked. This system is controlled by the body computer.

Functional description The boody computer M01 receives the control signals from the front door locks, at pins 24 and 34 (unlock/lock) for the left front door geared motor N50 and at pins 17 and 35 (unlock/lock) for the right front door geared motor N51 . In addition, the operation of the central locking can be activated using the remote control via the aerial P93 connected to pins 21 and 31 of connector C of the body computer. The locks communicate their opened or closed status to body computer M01 at connector A to the following pins: 8 for the left front door; 25 for right front door; 16 for the left rear door; 26 for the right rear door; 36 for the boot switch. The body computer M01 controls the cental locking system motors, from pins 16 and 18 of connector D in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 via the short circuit coupling D97 . The body computer M01 is supplied directly from the battery at pin A of connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

The front and rear door lock motors are operated simultaneously by using: - the key; - the front door switches (knobs); - the remote control. Lock operation: all four side doors lock simultaneously when one of the two front doors is locked with a key or remote control when all the doors are properly closed. Lock release operation: the door locks of the four side doors release when one of the two front doors is unlocked using the key or remote control. This control logic is controlled by the body computer node

Body computer M01 receives front door lock control signals at pins 24 and 34 (release/lock) for driver side gear motor N50 and at pins 17 and 35 (release/lock) for passenger side gear motor N51. Door lock operation may also be activated using the remote control via aerial P93 connected to pins 21 and 31 of connector C of the body computer. The locks communicate their open or closed status to body computer M01 at connector respectively at pins: - 8 driver side front door; - 25 passenger side front door; - 16 and 26 left and right sliding side doors; - 36 boot switch (with side-hinged door and up and over tailgate). Body computer M01 controls the door lock motors via short-circuiting junctions D97 from pins 16 and 18 connector D of under-dashboard junction unit B02. Body computer M01 is supplied directly from the battery at pin A of connector C of under-dashboard junction unit B02 . The direct power supply is protected by fuse F1 in engine compartment junction unit B01. Pins 8 and 9 of connector D of the body computer are earthed. With the key ON, if one of the doors is opened the door open warning light lights up on instrument panel E50. The supply lines that reach junction unit B02 via pin 11 connector E and pin A connector C also supply control panel E50 via two lines protected by fuses F37 and F53.

Description The front door electric windows are operated by switches in the middle of the facia. The operation is manual: the glass only goes up/down when the button is pressed. Both windows can only be operated when the ignition is ON. One some versions, if the button for operating the driver's electric window is pressed for more than half a second, the automatic operation is activated: the window stops when it reaches the end of travel position or if the button is pressed again. Operation is enabled for two minutes after turning the ignition from ON to OFF, only with the doors properly closed. The circuit for the electric windows is protected by two special fuses, one for the driver's side and one for the passenger side and is controlled by a specific relay located in the under-facia junction unit.

Functional description The operation of the front electric windows circuit is supplied by the electric windows relay R13 . It receives a supply from the direct line from the battery protected by fuse F2 housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 and is energized thanks to an earth signal leaving the body computer M01 . When energized, the relay supplies the control unit H90 (pins 5 and 3 connector C) via the two lines protected by fuses F47 and F48 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 (pins 20 and 19 connector E). The signals for the right electric window motor leave pins 6 and 7 of the control unit H90 , whilst those for the left electric window motor leave pins 1 and 4. Pins 2 and 8 are earthed. The supply for the body computer M01 is both controlled by the ignition (INT) and direct; at pins 11 of connector E and pin A of connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 , respectively. There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

Description There is a cigar lighter on the right of the ashtray. It has a ring nut which is lit up when the side lights are on. To operate the cigar lighter, simply press the knob: after a few seconds it pops out automatically, ready for use. On the left of the ashtray, on the other hand, there is an additional current socket which can be used for connecting instruments or equipment operating at 12 V. The circuit for the cigar lighter and the current socket is protected by a special fuse and controlled by an ignition-operated cut-out relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The sockets are only supplied when the ignition is switched ON.

Functional description Both the current socket in the dashboard P51 and the cigar lighter/current socket P50 receive a supply from the relay R12 via a line protected by fuse F44 both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . This line comes out of the control unit from pin 9 connector E and enters at pin 2 of P51 and pin 2 of P50 . The supply for the relay R12 comes from the direct line protected by fuse F1 housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 , whilst the supply for energizing the coil comes from the ignition switch H01 (INT/A). The earth is provided at pin 10 connector E of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 , at pin 3 of the cigar lighter / current socket P50 and at pin 3 of the current socket P51 . Both the ring nut for the current socket in the dashboard P51 and the ring nut for the cigar lighter P50 are lit up (both at pin 1 of each socket) when the side lights are on via an enablement signal coming out of the body computer M01 and protected by fuse F51 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 .

Description The front seat may be optionally fitted with a special heating system (consisting of two heater elements located in the cushion and squab): these heat the seat to ease the discomfort of entering a cold passenger compartment in very cold weather, e.g. when the car is left outside for long periods during winter. The seat heating circuit is operated by a switch on the actual seat and is protected by a special fuse and controlled by a relay which supplies other services controlled by the ignition.

Functional description The seat heating circuit is controlled by the relay R13 . It is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by fuse F2 housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . The coil energizing signal consists of an earth signal leaving pin 14 of connector X of the body computer M01 . The output supply signal from the relay R13 passes through fuse F45 and leaves the junction unit under the dashboard B02 from pin 4 connector D. This signal then reaches pin 2 of the heater pad I65 contained in the driver's seat. When the switch is turned on the supply reaches the heater pad O40 which heats up the seat. The heater pad is earthed via pin 1. The operation of the switch I65 also lights up the LED in the actual switch.

The front seats are available, on request, with a special heating system (comprising two heating elements located in the cushion and the backrest): this allows the seat to be heated to overcome the discomfort of cold passenger compartments in very harsh climates, e.g. when the car is left in the open for long periods in winter. The seat heating circuit is operated by a switch on the seat and protected by a special fuse and controlled by a relay that supplies other ignition-operated services.

The seat heating circuit is controlled by relay R13 of under-dashboard junction unit B02. This is supplied directly by the battery via a line protected by fuse F2 contained in engine compartment control unit B01. The coil excitation signal consists of an earth signal leaving pin 14 of connector X of body computer M01. The power supply leaving relay R13 flows through fuse F45 and leaves under-dashboard junction unit B02 from pin 4 connector D. This sigal then reaches pin 2 of switch I65 contained in the driver's side seat. When the switch is turned on, the power supply reaches heat pad O40, which heats the seat. Description The vehicle is equipped with a device which makes it possible to directly adjust the headlamp beam, according to the load, from the driver's seat. The headlamps are thus always aligned quickly and correctly. The adjustment device consists of a motor mounted on each of the two headlamps which tilts them as appropriate, lowering the light beam if the car is heavily laden, and raising it if the load decreases. A specific knob on the facia next to the dashboard is used to select the four possible positions. The position selected is shown in a display in the instrument panel. The device is only enabled when the dipped headlamps are switched on. The headlamp adjustment circuit is protected by the same fuses as the dipped beam headlamps circuit, located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

Functional description The front headlamps are adjusted via a selector in the left section of the instrument panel E50 . According to the value chosen using the special selector, E50 sends a voltage regulated signal to the junction unit under the dashboard B02 via pin 5 connector A. From there the signal is then sent to pin 1 connector A of the headlamp alignment motors control unit (pin F for the left headlamps F10 and right F11 ). The motors N30 and N31 in the headlamps contain a transducer that establishes the travel according to the regulation signal voltage. The supply for the headlamp alignment system located in the headlamps (right front F10 and left front F11 ) goes from the relay R1 , housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B02 , via a line protected by fuse F13 for the left headlamp and fuse F12 for the right headlamp both housed in the junction unit. When the dipped headlamps are activated, the body computer energizes the relay R1 which sends the supply to both the headlamp alignment motors from pin 3 connector A of the junction unit B02 entering pin D of the left headlamp F10 and pin 12 connector A of the same junction unit entering pin D of the right headlamp F11. At the same time, a signal is sent to switch on the dipped headlamps from pin 14 connector G of the junction unit B02 to pin 6 connector A of the instrument panel E50 . Both the instrument panel E50 and the body computer M01 receive supplies controlled by the ignition (INT) and direct: at pins 11 of connector E and pin A of connector C of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 , respectively. There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the engine compartment junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

The car is fitted with a device that allows the headlamp light beam to be adjusted for load directly from the driver's seat. The correct headlamp alignment is quickly achieved in this way. The adjustment device takes the form of a motor fitted on both dipped beams. It is able to tilt the headlamps to lower the light beam if the car is particularly loaded and raise the lamps when the load reduces. A control on the facia next to the instrument panel allows a choice of four possible positions. The selected position is displayed on the instrument panel display. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The headlamp alignment circuit is protectd by the dipped headlamp circuit fuses located in the underfacia junction unit.

The front headlamps are adjusted by means of two buttons on the left part of the instrument panel E50. When the ride adjustment buttons are pressed, E50 displays the number corresponding to the required position and sends a modulated voltage signal to the under-dashboard junctionj unit B02 via pin 6 connector A (for the Natural Power - 1596 16V BPW version - , pin 5 connector A). From here, the signal then leaves pin 1 connector A of control unit B02 for the headlamp alignment motors (pin 6 for the left headlamps and F10 and right headlamps F11). The correction motors inside the headlamps contain a transducer that estabilishes the travel to be completed on the basis of adjustment signal voltage. The power supply to the headlamp alignment system in the headlamps (front right F10 and front left F11) is taken from relay R1 in the under-dashboard junction unit B02 via a line protected by fuse F13. When the low beams are activated - pin 4 connector D - body computer M01 excites relay R1, which sends power to the two headlamp alignment motors from pin 2 connector A of junction unit B02 to left headlamp F10 and right headlamp F11. At the same time, a low beam activation signal is sent from pin 14 connector G of junction unit B02 to pin 7 connettore A of instrument panel E50 (for the Natural Power - 1596 16V BPW version - , pin 6 connector A). Instrument panel E50 and body computer M01 are supplied by an ignition-controlled supply (INT) via pin 11 connector E of control unit B02 and from the battery via a line protected by F1 of engine compartment control unit B01 that is connected to pin A connector C of the under-dashboard control unit. Pins 8 and 9 of connector D of the body computer are earthed.

Description The veihcle has a device that allows maximum ease of manoeuvring during parking; with reverse gear engaged, it indicates if the driver is approaching an obstacle that could be outside his field of vision, as illustrated in the diagram below. It operates according to the ultrasound sonar principle; four ultrasound transducers are located inside the rear bumper. They send signals to a control unit, which processes this information and determines the distance of possible obstacles. A loudspeaker controlled by the control unit emits an intermittent tone, proportional to the distance of the obstacle detected. The control unit is activated when reverse gear is engaged: under these conditions it energizes the transducers and prepares to receive signals from the sensors. The control unit emits a signal with an intermittent tone via the speaker with the frequency increasing as the rear of the vehicle approaches the obstacle. When the distance from the obstacle is less than 25 cm. the sound becomes acute and constant. If the distance measured from the obstacle increases or remains constant for 3 seconds (vehicle stationary) or reverse gear is engaged, the sound stops.

Functional description When reverse gear is engaged, the positive signal for switching on the rear lights ( See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS ) passes through the short circuit coupling D97A . The positive supply for the parking sensor control unit M84 reaches pin 1 of connector A from pin 10 of D97A . The negative supply for the control unit M84 reaches pin 8 of connector A from the dashboard earth C15C . The parking sensor speaker P44 receives signals from pins 2 and 10 of connector A for the parking control unit M84 ; pins 9 and 6 of the same connector, on the other hand, are bridged. The four parking sensors K97 are connected to sensor B of the control unit M84, respectively: to pins 5, 9, 12 sensor K97A ; to pins 7, 3, 10 sensor K97B ; to pins 1, 2, 6 sensor K97C ; to pins 8, 4, 11 sensor K97D .

The vehicle is equipped with a device that allows easy manoeuvring whilst parking: when reverse gear is engaged, it signals to the driver that an obstacle, which may be outside of the range of vision, is being approached. It works on a sonar ultrasound principle; four ultrasound transducers are located inside the rear bumper. They send signals to a control unit which processes this information determining the distance of possible obstacles. A speaker controlled by the control unit emits an intermittent sound, proportional to the distance of the obstacle detected. The control unit is activated with reverse gear engaged: in these conditions the transducers are energized and prepared to receive the signals from the sensors. The control unit produces a signal with intermittent tone via the speaker and the frequency increases as the rear of the vehicle gets closer to the obstacle. When the distance from the obstacle goes below 25 cm, the sound becomes high-pitched and constant. If the distance measured from the obstacle increases or remains constant for 3 seconds (vehicle stationary) or reverse gear is disengaged, the sound stops.

When reverse gear is engaged the positive signal (INT/A) for switching on the reversing lights moves via the junction unit uunder the dashboard B02 and supplies the parking sensors control unit M84 at pin 1 connector A via pin 8 connector D. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS The control unit M084 is earthed at pin 16 of connector A. The parking sensor speaker P44 receives signals from pins 2 and 10 of connector A of the parking control unit M84; pins 9 and 6 of the same connector are bridged. The control unit M84 provides a power supply and reference earth to the four parking sensors K97 from pins 6 and 1 of connector B respectively. The four front parking sensors K97 sends signals to connector B of the control unit M84: - to pin 5 the left external rear sensor K97E; - to pin 3 the left internal rear sensor K97F; - to pin 2 the right internal rear sensor K97G; - to pin 4 the right external rear sensor K97H;

Description The vehicle is available with a radio system fitted on request. The system consists of the following components: radio (CD / cassette player); radio supply cables; two front speakers in the dashboard; aerial; aerial coaxial cable. The radio circuit receives a direct supply from the battery (which allows tuning settings, security codes, etc. to be stored). The above line is protected by two fuses in the engine compartment junction unit and in the junction unit under the dashboard.

Functional description The operation of the radio system P20 is controlled by the body computer by the lines leaving pins 5 and 17 connector E of the junction unit B02 and entering at pins 1 and 3 connector A of the radio P20 , respectively. The radio is supplied directly (pin 7 connector A) by the battery via the line for fuse F1 housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 and protected by fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The radio P20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) (pin 4 connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The radio P20 receives the supply from pin 6 connector A for the interior lighting via the line controlled by the body computer M01 and protected bu fuse F51 of junction unit B02 . Connector B of the radio sends out cables with signals for the following speakers: right front in the dashboard P38 from pins 3 and 4 via the short circuit coupling D97 D; left front in the dashboard P37 from pins 5 and 6 via the short circuit coupling D97 D. Pin 5 connector A is connected to the aerial amplifier P25, whilst pin 8 connector A is earthed. The speaker P38 has the twin coil configuration when the preparation for a cell phone is fitted. The body computer is supplied via pin 11 connector E (supply controlled by the ignition) and pin A connector C (direct supply) of the junction unit B02 . There is a protective fuse F1 for the direct supply located in the junction unit B01 . Pins 8 and 9 connector D of the body computer are connected to earth.

The system consists of the following components: - car radio (CD / cassette player); - radio supply leads; - two front speakers located in the doors and two in the dashboard; - two rear speakers; - cables connecting the radio with the speakers; - aerial; - Subwoofer; - coaxial aerial lead. The subwoofer acoustic system is combined with the top of the range radio system. This system intensifies the low frequencies, giving excellent acoustic reproduction. The car radio system has a communication protocol with the electronic unit that manages the electrical equipment (body computer). When the radio is supplied the body computer reads the radio code and establishes whether or not it is activated. The radio circuit is supplied with the key ON and via a direct supply from the battery (which allows tuning, safety codes, etc. to be stored). The two power supply lines are protected by three fuses two of which are housed in the junction unit under the dashboard and the third is located in the engine compartment junction unit.

The operation of the radio system P20 is controlled by the body computer by lines coming out of pins 5 and 17 of connector E of junction unit B02 and entering at pins 1 and 3 connector A of the radio P20 respectively. The radio receives a direct power supply (pin 7 connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F1 housed in the engine compartment junction unit B01 and protected by fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02. The radio P20 receives ignition-controlled power (INT) (pin 4 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02. The radio P20 receives a power supply at pin 6 connector A with the side lights on for the interior lighting via the line controlled by the body computer M01 and protected by fuse F51 of junction unit B02. The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of the radio: - right front in the dashboard P38 and the door P36 from pins 3 and 4 via short circuiting coupling D97 D; - left front in the dashboard P37 and the door P35 from pins 5 and 6 via short circuiting coupling D97 B; - right rear P31 and subwoofer P92 (pins 2 and 5) from pins 1 and 2 via short circuiting coupling D97 E; - left rear P30 and subwoofer P92 (pins 1 and 4) from pins 7 and 8 respectively via short circuiting couplings D97 C and D97 E. Pin 5 connector A is connected to aerial amplifier P25 and to the subwoofer (pin 8) via the short circuiting coupling D97 D, whilst pin 8 connector A is earthed. The subwoofer receives a direct power supply (pin 3) via the line protected by fuse F36 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02. Pin 7, on the other hand, is earthed. Speaker P38 has a double coil configuration when preparation for a mobile phone is installed. The body computer is supplied via pin 11 connector E (ignition-controlled supply) and pin A connector C (direct supply) of the junction unit B02. There is a proective fuse F1 for the direct power supply located in the junction unit B01. Pins 8 and 9 of connector D of the body computer are earthed.

Description The vehicle is also available, on request, prepared for the installation of a cellular telephone. This preparation is configured as follows: dual function aerial (radio and cell phone); 'hands-free' speaker, located in the passenger side door (it is the same speaker as the radio with two connections: one for the radio and one for the cellular telephone 'hands-free' function); hands-free microphone located inside the front courtesy light. The connector for the cellular telephone has two supplies; one direct from the battery and one only with the ignition switched ON. The two lines are protected by fuses located in the junction unit under the dashboard and the junction unit in the engine compartment.

Functional description The radio phone connector D75 receives a direct supply (pin 9) from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 and is protected by fuse F1 of the engine compartment junction unit 0 B1 . It receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) at pin 7 via the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . The supply with the side lights on (POS) reaches the radio phone connector D75 at pin 8 via the line protected by fuse F51 of the junction unit under the dashboard B02 . Pin 10 of connector D75 is earthed, whilst cables leave pins 5 and 6 with signals for the right front speaker in the dashboard P38 at connector A. The radio phone connector D75 exchanges informatino via pins 4, 3 and 1 with the radio P20 if fitted (pins 7, 8 and 9 of connector C). A connection for the cell phone aerial is found near connector D75 .

The indicators and the warning lights that make up the on board instrumentation are grouped together in a single instrument which contains: - fuel level gauge with reserve warning light; - engine coolant temperature gauge (with overheating warning light) - rev counter; - speedometer; - warning lights; - digital display. The instrument panel is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The instrument panel shows a set of data on the digital display, namely: - mileometer/trip counter; - clock - Headlamp alignment corrector reading; - trip computer Fuel level: the Body Computer receives the signal from the sensor integrated in the pump assembly inside the fuel tank and processes it to guarantee suitable filtering/damping for the panel gauge, also managing the reserve warning light. The fuel level is displayed by an electronic circuit inside the module, which drives the gauge and also the reserve warning light (when the gauge is at 15% of the tank capacity). The internal logic also "dampens" the signal preventing fluctuations. Engine coolant temperature: this function involves the display of the engine coolant temperature in the instrument panel and the overheating warning light coming on by means of messages sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. Vehicle speed: The speedometer signal is supplied by a speedometer sensor. The body computer processes this signal and sends it to the instrument panel to display vehicle speed. For more details on the digital display, See E4080 TRIP COMPUTER Rev counter: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine rotation speed by means of the signal sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. Headlamp alignment correction keys on the left side of the facia can be used to adjust the front light headlamp light beam. See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR Engine oil pressure sensor: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine oil pressure warning light by means of the message sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. An ignition operated power supply (INT) from instrument E50 reaches pin 1 of connector A through body computer M01, pin 31 connector F, from a line protected by fuse F37 of under-dashboard junction unit B02. Instrument E50 is also supplied directly from the battery - pin 3 of connector A - via the body computer, pin 3 of connector D, from a line protected by fuse F53 contained in under-dashboard junction unit B02. The power supply to body computer M01 reaches pin 9 connector XY through under-dashboard junction unit B02 (pin 11 connector E) from ignition switch H01 (INT) and pin 18 of connector XY of body computer M01 through under-dashboard junction unit, directly from a battery protected by fuse F1 located inside engine compartment junction unit B01. Pins 8 and 9 of connector D of the body computer are earthed. Body computer M01 and control panel E50 communicate with one another to exchange information on the correct operation of the devices present in the vehicle respectively from pins 5 and 6 of connector D and pins 9 and 8 of connector A. Instrument panel E50 is also connected to earth via body computer M01 from pin 2 of connector A. Signals from handbrake switch I40 and brake fluid level sensor K25 are received from pin 14 connector A and pin 18 connector C of M01 respectively. Pins 4 and 15 of connector A of the body computer receives signals from the fuel level gauge located in the unit of pump N40: these signals, sent via the CAN network to the instrument panel, are processed by an internal electronic devices that manages the level gauge and reserve warning light in the instrument. Speedometer sensor K84 sends its signal directly to body computer M01 at pin 17 connector C. The signals are sent via the CAN line to instrument panel E50, to manage all information on vehicle speed, and to engine management control unit M10 to ensure its correct operation. Engine management control unti M10, pin 8 connector A receives a minimum engine oil pressure signal from sensor K30. This signal reaches instrument panel E50 via the CAN to make it possible to activate the warning light. In the same way, information on engine coolant temperature leaves sensor K36 and reaches engine control unit M10 at pins 54 and 62 of connector B. From there, it is then sent to instrument panel E50 to manage the gauge signal and also the excessive coolant temperature warning light, if necessary. RPM sensor K46 sends an engine rpm signal to engine control unit M10 at pins 53, 67 and 77 (screening) connector B; the control unit informs instrument panel E50 via the CAN network, which makes it possible to display the engine rpm. The information travels through the C-CAN line from pins 6 and 32 of connector A of M10 to pins 36 and 37 connector C of body computer M01. A headlamp alignment corrector control signal leaves pin 5 connector A of the instrument panel. See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR Signals are received from the AIR BAG control unit at pins 13, 14 and 15 of connector B for correct management of the various warning lights. See E7030 AIRBAG
